tools.name: add_obstacle
tools.description: Add an obstacle (solid block) to the FDS model. XB=[x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2] in metres.

tools.name: remove_obstacle
tools.description: Remove an obstacle by ID. In a BIM floor-plan project a derived object removes its BIM element: a wall piece removes the whole wall with its doors and windows (one piece of a diagonal wall = the whole wall), a slab removes the BIM slab, and a stair / elevator shaft wall or tread removes the whole stair or elevator.

tools.name: update_obstacle
tools.description: Update an existing obstacle by ID. Provide only fields to change. On a BIM-derived wall or slab (floor plan, add_wall, add_floor) the edit is applied to the BIM element: a move shifts the whole wall (all diagonal pieces) with its doors and windows, a new box size on an axis-aligned wall sets its centreline, thickness and height, surf_ids sets its surface. Stair / elevator objects are rebuilt from the element — use bim_update_stair / bim_update_elevator.

tools.name: set_fds_properties
tools.description: Update an obstacle's Runtime FDS Properties. Merge ANY fds_override fields and/or set is_fire_source/hrrpua/surf_ids. fds_override examples — fire: hrrpua_override, tmp_front, ramp_points, fire_area, fire_faces, ext_coeff; fuel/REAC: fuel_type, reac_co_yield, reac_soot_yield, reac_hcn_yield, reac_radiative_fraction; heat detector: activation_temp, rti, initial_temp; smoke: alpha_e, beta_e, alpha_c, beta_c; thermocouple: bead_diameter, emissivity, tc_density, specific_heat; sprinkler: spr_profile_id (shared spray profile), spr_spray_override (per-head FDS keys, e.g. {"particles_per_second":10000,"part":{"age":600}}; replaces the overrides — prefer spr_set_head_spray), spr_temp, spr_rti, k_factor (L/(min·bar^½)), operating_pressure (bar), flow_rate (L/min), spray_angle, particle_diameter (µm), spr_activation_time, spr_orientation (upright still 0,0,-1); HVAC: hvac_direction, volume_flow_rate, temperature, velocity, fan_curve, face_surfs, ramp_up_time. Read current values first with get_object_properties.

fds_override.description: fds_override fields to merge (any of the documented keys). Fire ignition (per fire surface): fire_ignition {mode:'immediate'|'time'|'temperature', time_s, temperature_c (°C, solid surface temperature of the fire faces), layers [{thickness, materials:[{matl_id, mass_fraction}]}] (non-reacting only; empty → fabric 1 mm + foam 50 mm), backing ('INSULATED')}; fire_surf_extra {KEY: raw FDS value} appended to the fire &SURF (wins over form keys; ID not allowed). More fire surfaces on one object (preset 'fire'): extra_fire_surfaces [{surf_id, hrrpua_override, tmp_front, ramp_id, ramp_points, fire_area, ext_coeff, fire_faces (6 booleans, must not overlap fds_override.fire_faces), fire_ignition, fire_surf_extra}] — each becomes its own &SURF; fuel/reaction keys stay shared. fire_surfaces multi-entry is legacy. fuel_type = a built-in fuel preset id (e.g. POLYURETHANE_FOAM) also fills spec/reac/yield/χr/heat-of-combustion keys not given in the call (GUI fuel list). Smoke detector: activation_obscuration (%/m). Thermocouple: tc_setpoint (°C trip). Easier object fires: add_fire(obstacle_id).

tools.name: add_hole
tools.description: Add a hole (opening in an obstacle) to the FDS model. XB defines the hole volume.

tools.name: remove_hole
tools.description: Remove a hole by ID. In a BIM floor-plan project a derived door / window / opening is removed from its wall (BIM opening), a slab hole is removed from its slab, and a stair / elevator door or shaft hole removes the whole stair or elevator.

tools.name: update_hole
tools.description: Update an existing hole by ID: move/resize it (xb) and/or rename it (new_id). Renaming keeps the opening as it is — use it to change the evacuation meaning without deleting the hole: a 'Door_'/'Window_' id is an evacuation exit, any other id is not (a floor-level opening at least 1.8 m tall stays walkable either way). On a BIM door / window the change is applied to the BIM opening (position along its wall, width, height, sill, id).

new_id.description: Rename the hole ('Door_D2' → 'D2' = no longer an exit, 'D3' → 'Door_D3' = exit). Must not clash with another hole id

tools.name: add_wall
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a wall by specifying start point, end point, height, and thickness. Automatically calculates the OBST bounding box. Points are [x,y] on the floor plane. The wall is tagged like a wall drawn in the 2D editor (furniture_name Wall). A diagonal wall becomes stair-step OBST pieces <id>_1, <id>_2 … grouped as wall_group=<id> (use <id> as wall_id for add_door / add_window). In a BIM floor-plan project it becomes a BIM wall with the same id (centreline = start/end, story from z_base) and is re-derived (joint-only end extension; a diagonal wall becomes one footprint polygon rasterised to the mesh grid instead of stair-step pieces); update_obstacle / transform_obstacle / remove_obstacle on any of its pieces edit or delete that whole wall.

tools.name: add_floor
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a floor slab (tagged furniture_name Floor like a 2D-editor floor). Specify x/y range and optional thickness. In a BIM floor-plan project it becomes a BIM slab with the same id on the story whose floor is at z.

tools.name: add_door
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a door opening in a wall. Specify the wall obstacle ID and door position/size. Creates a HOLE that cuts through the wall. Like a door drawn in the 2D editor, the hole id gets the prefix 'Door_' (e.g. id D1 → Door_D1), which makes it an evacuation exit (EVAC-002/003); pass evac_exit:false for an interior door that must not count as an exit (the id is then kept as given). The final id is in the result. Optional fire-model state (open default, closed, opens_at/closes_at with time_s) and closed-door crack leakage leak_area_m2 (see set_door_state / set_door_leakage); evacuation treats the door as a passage whatever its state. In a BIM floor-plan project a 'Door_' door becomes a BIM door of that wall (same id); an evac_exit:false id without the prefix stays a plain HOLE.

id.description: Door (hole) identifier — prefixed 'Door_' unless evac_exit is false or it already starts with Door_/Window_

wall_id.description: ID of the wall obstacle to cut (for a diagonal wall: its add_wall id / wall_group)

position.description: Position along the wall as fraction 0-1 (default 0.5 = center)

evac_exit.description: true (default): 'Door_' id = evacuation exit, like the 2D editor. false: keep the id as given — not an exit (EVAC-003)

state.description: Fire-model door state (default open = &HOLE; closed = wall kept; opens_at/closes_at need time_s)

leak_area_m2.description: Closed-door crack leakage area A_L [m²] (geometric gap area, localized leak) — written only when the state is not open

tools.name: add_window
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a window opening in a wall. Similar to add_door but with sill height. The hole id gets the prefix 'Win_' like windows from arch_import_building (e.g. W1 → Win_W1) — an opening in FDS, not an evacuation exit (EVAC-003). evac_exit:true uses 'Window_' instead (a 2D-editor window, which the evacuation model treats as an exit). The final id is in the result. In a BIM floor-plan project the window becomes a BIM window of that wall and keeps its id (Win_ stays Win_).

id.description: Window (hole) identifier — prefixed 'Win_' (or 'Window_' with evac_exit:true); an id already starting with Door_/Window_ is kept and is an exit

wall_id.description: ID of the wall obstacle to cut (for a diagonal wall: its add_wall id / wall_group)

evac_exit.description: false/omitted: 'Win_' id, not an exit. true: 'Window_' id = evacuation exit (2D-editor window)

tools.name: transform_obstacle
tools.description: Move / resize / rotate an existing obstacle (the 3D gizmo + property-panel SX/SY/SZ of the GUI). move = relative offset [dx,dy,dz] (m); place_at = absolute target point for `anchor` (default the XB centre); scale = absolute per-axis scale factors that stretch XB about its centre and rescale furniture voxels; rotation = [rx,ry,rz] degrees (kept as GUI metadata — &OBST itself stays axis-aligned, so a rotated furniture item is exported through its voxels). Combine as many as you need in one call. On a BIM-derived wall or slab the change is applied to the BIM element: moving one piece of a diagonal wall moves the whole wall with its doors and windows (a diagonal wall only moves); stair / elevator objects follow bim_update_stair / bim_update_elevator instead.

anchor.description: place_at reference: 'center' (default), 'min' (XB min corner), 'base' (XY centre at z_min)

tools.name: list_geoms
tools.description: List the &GEOM (triangulated cut-cell geometry) entries in the deck with triangle count, SURF_ID and bounding box.

tools.name: remove_geom

tools.name: add_fire
tools.description: Add a fire. Either a burner fire on a plane at xb (&FIRE, e.g. a floor patch) or, with obstacle_id, the object's fire setting (GUI Fire setting: burning faces, HRR, growth, extinguishing coefficient, ignition, fuel — replaces that object's earlier fire setting). Size: hrrpua (kW/m²) or hrr (total kW, divided by the burning area). Growth (auto-creates the RAMP): growth = NFPA t² preset with t_peak = √(Q_peak/α) from THIS fire's peak HRR, alpha = custom t² α (kW/s²), time_to_peak = t² reaching full HRR at that time, tau_q = FDS TAU_Q (>0 tanh, <0 t² to |τ|), or ramp_points. fuel_preset applies a built-in fuel (yields, χr, heat of combustion, formula): to the global &REAC for xb fires, to the object's fire chemistry for obstacle fires.

xb.description: Burner plane [x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2] (one zero-thickness axis, e.g. z1=z2 on the floor). Not with obstacle_id.

obstacle_id.description: Make this obstacle burn (fire setting on the object, like the GUI). Not with xb.

hrrpua.description: Peak heat release rate per unit area (kW/m²)

hrr.description: Peak total HRR (kW) instead of hrrpua — HRRPUA = hrr / burning area (xb plane area or the chosen faces).

ramp_id.description: RAMP ID: name for the generated curve, or (without a curve) an existing RAMP to use; "" clears the curve.

tmp_front.description: Burner surface temperature TMP_FRONT in °C (FDS unit; default 300 °C = GUI fire default; 20 = ambient, omitted from the deck). Not Kelvin.

ramp_points.description: Time-varying HRR curve as [[time_s, fraction], ...] where fraction is 0–1 of HRRPUA. Auto-creates a RAMP.

growth.description: NFPA t² preset (α = 0.003 / 0.012 / 0.047 / 0.188 kW/s²); reaches this fire's peak HRR at t_peak = √(Q/α).

alpha.description: Custom t² growth coefficient α in kW/s² (Q = α t² up to the peak HRR).

time_to_peak.description: Optional: t² curve reaching full HRR at this time (s) instead of √(Q/α).

tau_q.description: FDS TAU_Q style ramp (s): > 0 tanh(t/τ), < 0 (t/|τ|)² up to |τ|.

faces.description: obstacle_id only: burning faces 'xn','xp','yn','yp','zn','zp' (-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z). Default: the top face (zp) or the faces it already burns on.

ext_coeff.description: obstacle_id only: E_COEFFICIENT [m²/(kg·s)] — water suppression of this burning surface (0 = none).

ignition.description: obstacle_id only: when it starts burning — {mode:'immediate'|'time'|'temperature', time_s, temperature_c (solid surface temperature of the fire faces, °C; default 300)}.

fuel_preset.description: Built-in fuel preset id (e.g. POLYURETHANE_FOAM, WOOD_OAK, COTTON, NYLON, POLYPROPYLENE, PVC, PMMA, GASOLINE, PROPANE, METHANE, HEPTANE…).

fuel_preset.description: Built-in fuel preset id (e.g. POLYURETHANE_FOAM, WOOD_OAK, COTTON, NYLON, POLYPROPYLENE, PVC, PMMA, GASOLINE, PROPANE, METHANE, N-HEPTANE…)

tools.name: add_sprinkler
tools.description: Convenience: add a complete sprinkler head (FDS 6.10.1). Creates DEVC + PROP (QUANTITY=SPRINKLER LINK TEMPERATURE) + water-droplet PART (SPEC_ID=WATER VAPOR) from the project default spray profile (standard pendant K80: K 80 L/(min·bar^½), 1.0 bar, 68 °C, RTI 100, SPRAY_ANGLE 30/80, 10 m/s, 1000 µm, 5000 particles/s). Flow: give k_factor+operating_pressure (FDS derives Q=K√p), or flow_rate (optionally with pressure/K). K alone or pressure alone is rejected by FDS (ERROR 238). Upright heads also spray downward (only SMOKEVIEW_ID differs). profile_id picks another shared spray profile (e.g. ESFR or water mist from spr_upsert_spray_profile); spray / particle override any other &PROP / &PART key for this head (same keys as spr_upsert_spray_profile prop / part); activation opens it by time / CTRL / at t=0.

rti.description: Response Time Index (m·s)^½ (default 100; quick response ≤ 50; US (ft·s)^½ × 0.5521)

flow_rate.description: Flow rate in L/min (optional — default derives from K and pressure)

particles_per_second.description: Computational droplets per second per head (default 5000)

spray_angle.description: Spray angle [min,max] degrees from the axis (default [30,80]; 4 values = x/y ellipse)

droplet_diameter.description: Median volumetric droplet diameter D_v0.5 in μm (default 1000)

profile_id.description: Shared spray profile id (default: project default profile)

spray.description: Other &PROP keys for this head (spr_upsert_spray_profile.prop keys, e.g. {"spray_pattern_shape":"UNIFORM","offset":0.1})

particle.description: Other &PART droplet keys for this head (spr_upsert_spray_profile.part keys, e.g. {"distribution":"LOGNORMAL","sigma_d":0.6,"age":600})

activation.description: How the head opens: link (heat, default), time (DEVC TIME + SETPOINT), ctrl (CTRL_ID), initial (open at t=0).

ctrl_id.description: CTRL id (mode ctrl, or extra condition for link)

delay_s.description: s opening delay after link activation (dry/pre-action)

initial_state.description: INITIAL_STATE with time/ctrl (open first, close at SETPOINT)

tools.name: add_nozzle
tools.description: Convenience: add a Lagrangian-particle virtual fuel nozzle (e.g. hydrogen TPRD jet release). Automatically creates DEVC (QUANTITY=TIME, SETPOINT=0, ORIENTATION), PROP (MASS_FLOW_RATE / FLOW_RAMP / PARTICLE_VELOCITY / SPRAY_ANGLE / PARTICLES_PER_SECOND), PART (SPEC_ID / DIAMETER / MONODISPERSE / INITIAL_TEMPERATURE), the fuel SPEC (FORMULA + liquid-droplet properties taken from the built-in fuel database) and aligns REAC (FUEL / RADIATIVE_FRACTION / SOOT_YIELD / CO_YIELD) when no reaction is set yet.

mass_flow_rate.description: Mass flow rate at t=0 in kg/s (default 0.068)

spec_id.description: Fuel species (default 'HYDROGEN'). Known fuels get FORMULA + liquid properties automatically: HYDROGEN, METHANE, ETHANE, PROPANE, BUTANE, ETHYLENE, PROPYLENE, ACETYLENE, AMMONIA, METHANOL, ETHANOL, PROPANOL, ISOPROPANOL, ACETONE, BENZENE, TOLUENE, N-PENTANE, N-HEXANE, N-HEPTANE, N-OCTANE, ISOOCTANE, N-DECANE, DODECANE.

initial_temperature.description: Droplet initial temperature in °C (default: the fuel's boiling point −2~3°C, e.g. -255 for hydrogen)

flow_ramp_points.description: Mass-flow time series [[t,f],...] multiplying MASS_FLOW_RATE (blowdown decay etc.)

tools.name: add_heat_detector

activation_temp.description: Activation temperature (°C, default 57; ordinary 57, intermediate 68, high 79, extra high 93)

initial_temp.description: Link initial temperature (°C, GUI default 20 = ambient)

tools.name: add_smoke_detector

For the Heskestad LENGTH model use add_prop(CHAMBER OBSCURATION, length) + add_device(prop_id); a beam detector is add_device(PATH OBSCURATION, xb segment).

activation_obscuration.description: Alarm obscuration in %/m (FDS ACTIVATION_OBSCURATION; default 3.28 = standard; very sensitive 1.5, low sensitivity 6.65). %/ft × 3.28 = %/m.

tools.description: Add a CTRL control logic element. Override any field. Reference from devices via prop_id. tools.description: Set a uniform cell size (m); NI/NJ/NK are computed from the current domain extents. ⚠ Resets any multi-mesh deck to a single mesh. Use set_meshes / auto_multimesh to keep or build a multi-mesh deck.

tools.description: Auto-fit the mesh domain to the bounding box of all obstacles plus margin; recomputes NI/NJ/NK to keep the current cell size. A face holding a partial OPEN vent (e.g. in front of a door) stays where it is (margin 0 on that side) unless an obstacle sticks out; OPEN/MIRROR/PERIODIC vents on a face that moves follow it to the new boundary (same rule as set_mesh and the Mesh dialog). ⚠ Resets any multi-mesh deck to a single mesh. Use set_meshes / auto_multimesh to keep or build a multi-mesh deck.

tools.name: set_run_options
tools.description: Set simulation RUN options (RUN dialog): solver type (gpu / gpu_cutcell = octree cut-cell engine (beta), runs on the grid from the Mesh dialog cut-cell tab / cpu_openmp), CPU thread count, FDS output path.

tools.name: set_mesh
tools.description: Set the computational mesh resolution and domain extents (a single &MESH). ⚠ Resets any multi-mesh deck to a single mesh. Use set_meshes / auto_multimesh to keep or build a multi-mesh deck.

ni.description: Number of cells in X direction

nj.description: Number of cells in Y direction

nk.description: Number of cells in Z direction

tools.name: set_time
tools.description: Set the simulation end time.

tools.name: update_dump_config
tools.description: Update output dump intervals and settings. Other &DUMP keys (DT_CTRL, SIG_FIGS …): set_expert_settings.

dt_bndf.description: Boundary (.bf) output interval (s). Omit or 0 to leave DT_BNDF out of the deck; the GPU engine then writes BNDF at the DT_SLCF interval.

dt_restart.description: Restart/checkpoint interval (s). The GPU engine now writes a resumable checkpoint at this cadence.

nframes.description: FDS NFRAMES (default 1000): any DT_* left unset is filled with (T_END-T_BEGIN)/NFRAMES. Lower it to cut slice/smoke frame count and disk usage on long runs.

tools.name: set_turbulence_model
tools.description: Set the turbulence model. Options: DEARDORFF (default), VREMAN, WALE, CONSTANT_SMAGORINSKY. Model constants (C_SMAGORINSKY, C_VREMAN, C_WALE, PR_T, SC_T …) and other expert keys: set_expert_settings.

tools.name: set_simulation_mode
tools.description: Set simulation mode: LES, VLES, SVLES, or DNS

tools.name: set_numerics
tools.description: Set numerical stability controls (time step and advection scheme). Use this when a run diverges, produces NaN, or when matching CPU FDS settings. dt/lock_time_step map to &TIME; the rest to &MISC. Omitted fields keep the FDS default for the current SIMULATION_MODE. particle_global sets the particle/spray-wide keys (&MISC POROUS_FLOOR, PARTICLE_CFL(_MAX/_MIN), CNF_CUTOFF, NEAR_WALL_PARTICLE_INTERPOLATION; &DUMP MAXIMUM_PARTICLES, DT_PART); particle_global_unset returns keys to the FDS default. Other &TIME/&MISC keys (VN_MIN, RESTRICT_TIME_STEP …): set_expert_settings.

particle_global.description: Particle-wide FDS settings for all nozzles (&MISC POROUS_FLOOR / PARTICLE_CFL… , &DUMP MAXIMUM_PARTICLES / DT_PART).

porous_floor.description: &MISC — droplets reaching the domain floor (ZMIN) are removed (FDS default true)

dt.description: Initial time step [s]. Omit to let the solver derive it from CFL_MAX*min(dx)/sqrt(g*H).

lock_time_step.description: Freeze dt (disable CFL adaptation). Requires dt. Standard remedy for a diverging case.

cfl_max.description: CFL upper bound (FDS VLES default 1.0). Lower it (e.g. 0.5) to stabilise.

cfl_min.description: CFL lower bound (default 0.8) — below this the solver grows dt.

vn_max.description: Von Neumann (diffusion) stability limit. VLES 1.0 / LES 0.8 / DNS 0.5.

flux_limiter.description: Scalar advection limiter. VLES default SUPERBEE, LES/DNS default CHARM. The GPU engine implements CHARM; only MP5 is unsupported and falls back to CHARM with a warning.

tools.name: get_numerics
tools.description: Read the current numerical stability settings (time step, CFL/VN limits, flux limiter).

tools.name: set_ambient
tools.description: Set the ambient (initial atmosphere) conditions written to &MISC: TMPA (ambient temperature °C), HUMIDITY (%RH), Y_CO2_INFTY (background CO2 mass fraction). The GPU engine reads all three. For any other &MISC key prefer set_expert_settings (validated); `extra` writes KEY=VALUE verbatim (e.g. P_INF, GVEC). Pass null for a key to drop it and fall back to the FDS default (TMPA 20°C, HUMIDITY 40%).

extra.description: Raw &MISC entries as 'KEY=VALUE' (e.g. ["P_INF=101325."]). Replaces any entry with the same KEY.

tools.name: get_simulation_settings
tools.description: Read every simulation setting in one call: time (T_BEGIN/T_END), SIMULATION_MODE, turbulence model, numerics (DT/CFL/VN/flux limiter), ambient &MISC values, output dump intervals and Plot3D quantities, and the mesh deck size. Use it before changing settings so you know what is already explicit. Every explicit FDS global key per group with GPU support: get_expert_settings.

tools.name: list_raw_namelists
tools.description: List the raw namelist lines carried through unchanged (&RADI, &PRES, &COMB, &MULT, &HVAC, …) — settings the GUI has no dialog for but the deck and the engine keep. Pressure zones (&ZONE) are not raw lines: see list_pressure_zones.

tools.name: add_raw_namelist
tools.description: Add a raw namelist line emitted verbatim just before &TAIL — for namelists the GUI does not model (e.g. "&MULT ID='M1', DX=1., I_UPPER=3 /"). Must start with & and end with /. For the global groups &RADI/&PRES/&COMB/&WIND/&CLIP prefer set_expert_settings (validated, one line per group). Use the dedicated tools for anything the GUI does model (&MESH/&OBST/&VENT/&SURF/&REAC/&DEVC/&CTRL/&SLCF/&BNDF/&DUMP/&TIME/&MISC; &ZONE → add_pressure_zone / set_zone_leakage) — a duplicate namelist is an FDS error. &MOTION, &TRNX/&TRNY/&TRNZ, &CSVF, &ISOF, &SM3D and &RADF lines are not kept verbatim: they become project settings (checked like the GUI) and then do not appear in list_raw_namelists / remove_raw_namelist — read them with preview_fds and change or remove them with fds_apply_text.

tools.name: remove_raw_namelist
tools.description: Remove a raw namelist line by its index from list_raw_namelists.

tools.name: list_meshes
tools.description: List the current &MESH deck (multi-mesh or the single mesh) with per-mesh XB, IJK, cell size, cell count and coarse/fine ratio, plus totals and a self-check for overlap / gaps / non-cubic cells. Read this before set_meshes, slice_mesh or merge_meshes so index numbers refer to the right mesh.

tools.name: set_meshes
tools.description: Replace the whole &MESH deck with an explicit list of meshes (multi-mesh). Passing a single mesh reverts the project to single-mesh mode. config.mesh (the union bounding box) and the OPEN-boundary vents are kept consistent by the app. Engine constraints (engine multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify with list_meshes; for shape-driven placement prefer auto_multimesh.

meshes.description: Meshes that together tile the domain, in order.

id.description: Optional mesh ID (must be unique, e.g. M1)

tools.name: slice_mesh
tools.description: Split one mesh into two at a plane (multi-mesh cutter). The coordinate snaps to that mesh's own grid lines, cell size is preserved on both halves, and OPEN vents crossing the plane are split too. Slicing the single mesh turns the project into a multi-mesh deck. Use list_meshes for index numbers.

axis.description: Axis normal to the cut plane

coord.description: Cut position (m). Snapped to the nearest grid line of that mesh.

tools.name: merge_meshes
tools.description: Merge several meshes back into one (inverse of slice_mesh). Succeeds only when the selected meshes do not overlap and their union is exactly a box. When their cell sizes differ, `choice` picks which size the result uses; the union must divide into a whole number of those cells. Use list_meshes for index numbers.

indices.description: Mesh indices to merge (2 or more)

choice.description: Cell size to keep when the meshes differ: 'coarse' (larger cells, fewer) or 'fine'.

tools.name: auto_multimesh
tools.description: Build a multi-mesh deck from the OBSTRUCTION geometry. It measures the fluid gap everywhere (obstacles minus HOLEs, so doorways stay open), gives narrow places 3+ cells across and open places the default wide cell, then merges equal-size regions into boxes cut on obstacle faces so walls stay on mesh boundaries. Wall slabs up to 2 cells thick are absorbed into a neighbour. Cell sizes are quantised to min_cell x 2^k; an overlapping, gapped or misaligned deck is refused, not committed. The domain may grow to a multiple of the coarsest cell; OPEN vents follow. Engine constraints (engine multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify the result with list_meshes.

min_cell.description: Finest cell size (m), e.g. 0.05. Must be > 0; it is the bottom of the 2^k ladder.

max_cell.description: Coarsest cell size (m), e.g. 0.2. Rounded DOWN to min_cell x 2^k.

tools.name: auto_cutcell_mesh
tools.description: Build a cut-cell multi-mesh deck from &GEOM triangulated shapes (plus OBSTs). Cells shrink where the fluid gap is narrow (gap / gap_cells), the GEOM surface band always gets the finest cell so the engine keeps its cut-cell wall physics there, sharp curvature gets one level finer, and levels change at most 2:1 between neighbouring blocks. Cell sizes are min_cell x 2^k. If the deck has no GEOM this is identical to auto_multimesh. Over budget it relaxes curvature, buffer, gap_cells, then raises min_cell and reports what it changed; a gapped, overlapping or misaligned deck is refused. Engine constraints (engine multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify with list_meshes.

min_cell.description: Finest cell size (m), e.g. 0.05 — used on the GEOM surface band and in narrow gaps.

max_cell.description: Coarsest cell size (m), e.g. 0.2. Rounded DOWN to min_cell x 2^k.

gap_cells.description: Minimum cells across a narrow gap (default 4, floor 3).

tools.name: add_material

specific_heat_ramp.description: SPECIFIC_HEAT_RAMP — &RAMP id with points [T °C, c kJ/(kg·K)]; "" removes it

id.description: Current material ID (project or built-in library)

new_id.description: New material ID (unique, no quotes, ≤ 60 bytes)

tools.name: preview_material_kinetics
tools.description: Read-only: evaluate a material's pyrolysis exactly as FDS 6.10.1 does — effective A/E (derived from REFERENCE_TEMPERATURE or given), peak temperature and rate at the heating rate, FDS GET_TMP_REF, a virtual TGA (normalized mass and mass-loss rate vs temperature, 40 points, residue chain included), and the FDS input checks (MATL-001…011). Liquids: equilibrium vapor fraction vs temperature.

heating_rate.description: TGA heating rate [K/min] (default: the reaction HEATING_RATE or 5)

x_o2.description: Oxygen volume fraction for N_O2>0 reactions (default 0.2095)

tools.name: list_pressure_zones
tools.description: Read-only: pressure zones (&ZONE) in FDS zone-number order with seed XYZ and the region FDS 6.10.1 flood-fills from each seed (volume, cells, sealed or connected to an OPEN boundary), the zones FDS creates by itself for other sealed regions, zone-pair leakage (&ZONE LEAK_AREA with C_d, Δp_ref, n), door fire states and door leakage as written to the deck, and the region check: seed outside the mesh or inside a solid, two zones in one region (ERROR 872) or meeting at a mesh boundary (ERROR 873), leakage ignored because no LEAK_PATH surface carries it or its faces touch only one zone of the pair, fire in a sealed region without leakage, door leak geometry (thin wall, no lintel above a timed door → ERROR 564).

tools.name: add_pressure_zone
tools.description: Add an explicit pressure zone (&ZONE ID, XYZ). Give xyz [m] — a point in the gas of the compartment, not inside a wall or furniture — or room {story_id, x, y} to seed at that plan point at the story floor + min(1 m, half the story height) (a point inside a closed wall polygon links the zone to that room), or auto_zone = the number of an automatic FDS zone from list_pressure_zones to promote it (seed = a gas cell of that region). Zones are numbered in list order; LEAK_AREA indices and numeric LEAK_PATH are recomputed on export, so ids are the references. Returns the region FDS will assign (volume, sealed or open) and errors: seed in a solid, two zones in one region (ERROR 872 — doors between them must be closed or timed). A sealed zone without leakage pressurizes with the fire: add set_zone_leakage or door leakage.

xyz.description: Seed point [x, y, z] in m

room.description: Seed from a plan point on a story instead of xyz

auto_zone.description: Promote this automatic FDS zone number (list_pressure_zones auto_zones) instead of xyz / room

tools.name: update_pressure_zone
tools.description: Change a pressure zone: new_id renames it and updates every reference (zone-pair leakage, door leak sides, surface LEAK_PATH, raw &SURF LEAK_PATH_ID); xyz moves the seed point [m]; color changes the display colour; position moves it to that FDS zone number (1-based list order, like the ▲▼ buttons). Returns the re-checked region.

xyz.description: New seed point [x, y, z] in m

tools.name: remove_pressure_zone
tools.description: Remove a pressure zone. Its zone-pair leakage is deleted, door leak sides that pointed to it return to auto, and surface leak paths to it are cleared (listed in the result). The region becomes an automatic FDS zone (or part of the ambient) again; the other zones are renumbered on export.

tools.name: set_zone_leakage
tools.description: Set the leakage between a pressure zone and another zone or the ambient (&ZONE LEAK_AREA(n), one value per pair; area_m2 = 0 deletes the pair). FDS 6.10.1 ignores LEAK_AREA unless a surface with LEAK_PATH for that pair is on an obstruction or vent: give leak_surface (a general surface that becomes the leak path — assign it to the walls between the zones with assign_surface) or use door leakage with model zone_path. basis fills C_d / Δp_ref / n; explicit values override. Instead of area_m2, wall_ratio {wall_area_m2, ratio | preset} = wall area × leakage ratio (wall area defaults to room perimeter × story height for a room-linked zone). new_leak_surface:true creates the leak-path surface LEAK_<zone>_<to>. For one door use set_door_leakage instead.

wall_area_m2.description: Wall area [m²] (default: room perimeter × story height)

tools.name: set_door_state

Evacuation still treats every door as a passage and exit. Door leakage is written only when the state is not open; a timed or controlled door keeps a localized leak vent on the lintel above it (FDS ERROR 564 on the removable filler).

tools.name: set_door_leakage

id.description: Hole ID (e.g. Door_D1) or door furniture obstacle ID

enabled.description: Leakage on/off (default on when an area is given)

preset.description: Standard preset id (NFTC 501A / EN 12101-6 / NFPA 105 — unverified values)

discharge_coefficient.description: DISCHARGE_COEFFICIENT C_d (default from basis, FDS default 1)

basis.description: Area definition: fds_ela4 (ELA, C_d 1, 4 Pa — FDS default), gap_orifice (geometric gap area NFTC 501A / EN 12101-6, C_d 0.64), eqla10 (EqLA, C_d 0.611, 10 Pa, n 0.65), custom

clearFields.description: Remove these nozzle fields (requiredPressure → back to the design default)

tools.description: Remove a sprinkler head by ID

tools.name: spr_remove_water_source
tools.description: Remove a water source by ID

tools.name: spr_set_defaults
tools.description: Set default pipe diameter, pipe standard and K-factor for new pipes/heads, the project default spray profile, the hydraulic minor-loss options (fittings/valves by NFPA 13 equivalent length, large-size 250-600 mm table), and the DESIGN BASIS: default required pressure per nozzle kind (requiredPressureClosed / requiredPressureOpen, MPa), operation (auto = zone deluge when zones exist / all_open / zone_deluge), includeClosedHeads (false = only open nozzles and drains discharge), drainCd, velocity warning / fail limits.

defaultMaterial.description: Default pipe standard for new pipes

defaultKFactor.description: Default K-factor (new nozzles and drains — drain hole = sprinkler orifice)

requiredPressureClosed.description: Default required pressure of closed sprinklers [MPa] (0.1)

requiredPressureOpen.description: Default required pressure of open nozzles [MPa] (0.1)

includeClosedHeads.description: Closed sprinklers discharge in the calculation (default true)

largeSizeTable.description: Use the 250-600 mm fitting equivalent-length table (new projects on)

defaultSprayProfileId.description: Project default spray profile — new heads and heads without an explicit profile follow it

includeMinorLosses.description: Include fitting and valve losses in the hydraulic calculation (default true)

conservativeRunLoss.description: Add the conservative Korean-textbook straight-run loss for tees/crosses/wyes (default false = NFPA 13 run loss 0)

taperedReducer.description: Treat reducers as tapered (loss 0, NFPA 13 rule 10) instead of reducing couplings/bushings (default false)

drawRoute.description: GUI pipe drawing route: straight, or L-shape with an automatic elbow node (X first / Y first)

tools.name: spr_run_calc
tools.description: Run the hydraulic calculation. mode design (default) = scenarios "all" and one per deluge zone, each at the actual water source AND the inverse REQUIRED SOURCE PRESSURE (minimum source pressure so every participating nozzle reaches its own required pressure; drains always open; closed valves exclude pipes) with the governing nozzle and a pump check. mode calc = the classic single forward calculation. Read the results with spr_get_results (next round) — detail lines gives the table by line number.

scenarios.description: design: which scenarios (default both = 'all' + every zone)

inverse.description: design: solve the required source pressure (default true)

tools.name: spr_list_summary
tools.description: Get the sprinkler status (read-only): pipe network nodes / pipes / fittings / risers with ids, sprinkler heads with their spray profile and override count, the spray profile library with usage. include_presets lists spray presets (standard, quick response, ESFR, residential, water mist low/intermediate/high pressure); profile_id returns one profile with every FDS key and the heads using it.

include_presets.description: Also list the spray presets (keys for spr_upsert_spray_profile.preset)

profile_id.description: Show this spray profile in full (FDS keys, usage)

tools.name: spr_auto_layout
tools.description: Automatically build a complete, calculable sprinkler pipe network in a rectangular area. mode grid (default): a water source node (city water) at the (xMin, yMin) corner, a cross-main along x = xMin, one branch line per row, sprinkler nodes on a grid with heads, and every connecting pipe. mode rules: the drawing-wizard layout engine (NFSC 103 / NFPA 13 practice — every floor point within coverageRadius of a head behind no wall, L_b²+L_h² ≤ (2r)², wall clearance, main → 90° branches → heads, one branch per tee) with walls from full-height obstacles on the story (or walls / the area outline), the main along mainPoints (default the centre line of the long side); a city-water source at the main start, or connectToNodeId joins an existing node (riser top). Follow with spr_run_calc and spr_apply_to_fds to put the sprinklers into the FDS model.

z.description: Sprinkler height (m). Default grid 2.8; rules = the story ceiling (zMin + height) or the connectToNodeId height

spacingX.description: grid: X spacing between sprinklers (m, default 3.0)

spacingY.description: grid: Y spacing between sprinklers (m, default 3.0)

floorIndex.description: Story id (draw_list_stories id). Default: the story that contains z

mainDiameter.description: Main pipe nominal size (mm, default max(50, default size)); branches use the default size

walls.description: rules: wall segments [[x1,y1,x2,y2],…] (m) instead of the obstacles

connectToNodeId.description: rules: connect the main start to this existing pipe node (no new source)

rules.description: rules options (wizard defaults): coverageRadius 2.3 m (r), wallClearance 0.6, minMainClearance 0.5, minHeadSpacing 1.8, branchAngle ortho|free, firstBranchOffset 1, maxNozzlesPerBranch 1, minBranchLength 0.4, maxBranchLength (none), exclusionZones [[[x,y],…],…]

tools.name: spr_set_nozzles
tools.description: Set nozzle data on many pipe-network nozzles at once — choose them with all / headIds / nodeIds / zone / lineNo / kind (filters combine). Sets kind (closed sprinkler | open nozzle | drain), K, the REQUIRED DISCHARGE PRESSURE per nozzle (MPa; clearRequiredPressure = back to the design default), zone (deluge zone), lineNo, disabled, nozzleModel, drain orifice diameter (K recalculated). One undo step.

lineNo.description: Select nozzles on this line number

clearRequiredPressure.description: Use the design default required pressure again

disabled.description: Exclude from / include in the calculation

tools.name: spr_set_valves
tools.description: Open / close valves (closed valve → that pipe is excluded from the calculation, downstream is isolated) and set their tag or zone (zone valve = open only in the "all" scenario and its own zone scenario). Choose with pipeId (+ index, default all valves on the pipe), tag, or zone.

index.description: Valve index on the pipe (spr_list_summary order); default every valve on the pipe

tag.description: Select valves with this tag (e.g. WS-11U)

zone.description: Select zone valves of this zone

tools.name: spr_add_drain
tools.description: Add a drain hole (always-open orifice, flow = K√P, no required pressure): on a pipe at position (splits it with a new branch node), on an existing node, or at a free point. K defaults to the project nozzle K (drain hole = sprinkler orifice); orificeDiameterMm converts with Cd 0.62.

pipeId.description: Put the drain on this pipe (new branch node)

position.description: Position along the pipe from its start node 0..1 (default 0.5)

nodeId.description: Or put it on this node

disabled.description: Closed drain valve (not in the calculation)

tools.name: spr_set_pipes
tools.description: Change many pipes at once: choose all / pipeIds / lineNo / runOf (the run through that pipe up to branches); set the pipe standard (material, C resets unless keepC), Hazen-Williams C, line number. One undo step per change. Out-of-standard sizes keep their size (inner diameter = nominal) and are reported.

lineNo.description: Select pipes with this line number

runOf.description: Select the run through this pipe id (stops at branches, ends and the source)

material.description: Pipe standard id (schedule included). Building: KSD3507 | CPVC | STS304 | ASTM_SCH40. Marine/plant: JIS_G3454_STPG_SCH40/SCH80, KS_D3562_SPPS_SCH40/SCH80, JIS_G3452_SGP, JIS_G3459_SUS_SCH10S/SCH40, ASTM_A53_A106_SCH40/SCH80, DIN86019_CUNI10FE (CuNi 90/10), … (enum). C resets to the standard default unless cFactor is given.

keepC.description: Keep each pipe C when changing the standard

tools.name: spr_upsert_spray_profile
tools.description: Create, update or delete a shared SPRAY PROFILE — the FDS 6.10.1 &PROP+&PART template (flow, spray pattern, droplet size distribution, breakup, drag, evaporation, surface film, parcels) that sprinkler and water-mist heads reference. Omit id (or give a new id) to create: it starts from `preset` (default std_pendant_k80) or `copy_from`. With an existing id, `preset` overwrites its values, prop/part merge keys and unset_prop/unset_part return keys to the FDS default. Presets: standard, quick response, ESFR, residential, water mist low (12 bar) / intermediate (21 bar) / high (70-100 bar) — spr_list_summary {include_presets:true}. assign_to links heads to the profile (pipe heads take its K, activation temperature and RTI). Every edit is checked like FDS (K or pressure alone = ERROR 238, no DIAMETER = 214, equal SPRAY_ANGLE = 231, bad EVAP_MODEL = 224) for the profile and every head using it; on error nothing changes. Per-head overrides: spr_set_head_spray.

id.description: Profile id. Existing = update; new or omitted = create

preset.description: Preset to start from (new) or to overwrite the values with (existing)

copy_from.description: New profile = copy of this profile id

prop.description: FDS 6.10.1 &PROP spray keys (lowercase FDS names, FDS units). Unset = FDS default.

flow_mode.description: Which flow keys are written: k_p = K+pressure (FDS Q=K√p) | q_p | q_only | q_k | q_k_p | k_pressure_ramp | mass (MASS_FLOW_RATE) | hydraulic (pipe-network Q_i/P_i)

velocity_mode.description: direct = PARTICLE_VELOCITY; orifice = FDS derives v from ORIFICE_DIAMETER

hydraulic_pressure_correction.description: Pipe-network heads: scale D∝(p0/P)^(1/3), v∝√(P/p0) with the calculated head pressure

flow_ramp_id.description: Existing project RAMP id (T = s after activation, F = flow fraction)

spray_angle.description: [min,max] deg from the spray axis, or 4 values (x pair, y pair) for an ellipse; FDS default 60,75

part.description: FDS 6.10.1 &PART water-droplet keys (lowercase FDS names; diameters in µm). Unset = FDS default.

cnf.description: [[diameter µm, cumulative NUMBER fraction 0..1], ...] user distribution

adhere_to_solid.description: INTEGER 1 = stick to solids, -1 = do not (a logical is FDS ERROR 101)

horizontal_velocity.description: m/s film speed on horizontal surfaces (default 0.2)

vertical_velocity.description: m/s film speed on vertical surfaces (default 0.5)

kill_diameter.description: µm (written for MONODISPERSE parts only — 6.10.1 bug)

advanced_prop.description: Extra raw &PROP 'KEY=VALUE' entries (checked against the FDS 6.10.1 key list); [] clears

fds_prop_id.description: Fixed &PROP ID written for this profile ("" = derive)

fds_part_id.description: Fixed &PART ID written for this profile (for PART_ID in AMPUA/MPUV devices; "" = derive)

make_default.description: Make it the project default profile (new heads and heads without a profile follow it)

delete.description: Delete the profile (refused while heads use it or if it is the last one)

all.description: every sprinkler head in the project (pipe network, obstacle and DEVC sprinklers)

group.description: sprinkler interlock/deluge group id or name — all its members

network_of_node.description: pipe node id — every head in the pipe network connected to it

node_ids.description: pipe-network sprinkler node ids (all heads on them)

clear_overrides.description: Also drop the heads' per-head spray overrides

keep_head_values.description: Pipe heads keep their own K / activation temperature / RTI

tools.name: spr_set_head_spray
tools.description: Set per-head spray settings on one or many sprinkler heads — pipe-network heads, obstacle sprinklers and DEVC sprinklers alike (the GUI spray dialog "this head only" path). Pick heads with all / group (interlock or deluge group) / network_of_node / head_ids / node_ids / obstacle_ids / device_ids. profile_id links them to a shared profile (pipe heads take its K, activation temperature and RTI unless keep_head_values). prop / part override single FDS keys for these heads only; inherit lists keys to hand back to the profile (prop/part keys or orientation, rotation, pipe_index, activation); reset drops every override. orientation / rotation / pipe_index / activation are DEVC values. head_type applies to pipe heads (upright still sprays down). All heads are checked first; if any would be an FDS error nothing changes. Pipe heads whose K changed need spr_run_calc then spr_apply_to_fds.

all.description: every sprinkler head in the project (pipe network, obstacle and DEVC sprinklers)

group.description: sprinkler interlock/deluge group id or name — all its members

network_of_node.description: pipe node id — every head in the pipe network connected to it

node_ids.description: pipe-network sprinkler node ids (all heads on them)

profile_id.description: Link the heads to this spray profile

keep_head_values.description: With profile_id: pipe heads keep their own K / activation temperature / RTI

reset.description: Drop every per-head spray override first (pipe heads: K / activation / RTI back to the profile)

prop.description: Per-head &PROP overrides — same keys and units as spr_upsert_spray_profile.prop. pressure_ramp:"network" computes the PRESSURE_RAMP rows (open heads → bar) from the pipe network for the selected pipe heads (flow_mode k_pressure_ramp)

part.description: Per-head &PART droplet overrides — same keys and units as spr_upsert_spray_profile.part

inherit.description: Keys to remove from the heads so they follow the profile again

orientation.description: DEVC ORIENTATION spray axis (default [0,0,-1]; sidewall e.g. [1,0,0])

pipe_index.description: DEVC PIPE_INDEX (pipe network number for PRESSURE_RAMP / OPEN NOZZLES)

activation.description: How the head opens: link (heat, default), time (DEVC TIME + SETPOINT), ctrl (CTRL_ID), initial (open at t=0).

ctrl_id.description: CTRL id (mode ctrl, or extra condition for link)

delay_s.description: s opening delay after link activation (dry/pre-action)

initial_state.description: INITIAL_STATE with time/ctrl (open first, close at SETPOINT)

tools.name: spr_set_group
tools.description: Create, update or delete a sprinkler INTERLOCK / DELUGE group (GUI sprinkler group dialog; written as FDS 6.10.1 &CTRL wiring). interlock: when any member opens by its own link, every member opens. deluge: all members open together when any trigger trips (heat / smoke detector, thermocouple with a setpoint, DEVC with SETPOINT); members do not open by their own link. Members are FDS sprinklers — obstacle / DEVC sprinklers and pipe-network heads AFTER spr_apply_to_fds — chosen with all / group / network_of_node / head_ids / node_ids / obstacle_ids / device_ids (member_action replace = default | add | remove). Omit id (or give a new id) to create; delete=true removes. spr_list_summary lists the groups.

id.description: Group id or name — existing = update, new or omitted = create

all.description: every sprinkler head in the project (pipe network, obstacle and DEVC sprinklers)

group.description: sprinkler interlock/deluge group id or name — all its members

network_of_node.description: pipe node id — every head in the pipe network connected to it

node_ids.description: pipe-network sprinkler node ids (all heads on them)

member_action.description: How the selected heads change the members (default replace)

triggers.description: deluge triggers: detector obstacle ids or DEVC ids/uids (replaces the list; [] clears)

delay.description: Opening delay after the group trips (s, 0 = none)

tools.name: spr_apply_to_fds
tools.description: Apply the hydraulic pipe-network sprinklers to the FDS model: for every sprinkler node (with a head and calc results from spr_run_calc), creates/replaces DEVC (SPRINKLER LINK TEMPERATURE) + PROP + PART entries using the calculated nozzle flow and pressure. Run spr_run_calc first. scenario / at pick the design scenario whose flows are written (GUI result window view switch); default = the result shown (after spr_run_calc: 'all' at the actual source).

scenario.description: 'all' or 'zone:<zone>' — write that scenario's nozzle flows / pressures

at.description: With scenario: actual source (default) or inverse design point

tools.name: spr_analyze_drawing
tools.description: Read a sprinkler / water-spray piping drawing (.dxf, .dwg, .pdf, .zip of drawings, .png/.jpg) and recognise a candidate pipe network. Isometric (ISO) drawings: scale from DIMENSION entities, pipe linetype, bends, flange/valve gaps bridged, nozzle stems, line-number / reducer / valve labels, 3D reconstruction (X,Y horizontal, Z up, inlet = origin), nominal sizes from labels and flange rings. Plan drawings: pipe layers + head symbols at one height. Returns a summary with candidateId, open ends (drain candidates), reference (dashed, other-system) labels, exclusion hints, runs and ambiguities to ask the user about. Attached chat files arrive as "[첨부 도면] name path=… candidateId=…". PDFs with outlined text set needsVision (read the page image instead). show=segments|nodes|runs|tags|components lists details (ids, offset, limit, component). Then call spr_import_network.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the drawing file

candidateId.description: Id from an earlier analysis or the chat attachment (re-use without re-reading)

options.description: Re-analysis options: projection (isometric|plan), pipeLinetypes / referenceLinetypes / detailLinetypes (DXF linetype names), layers / excludeLayers, scaleMmPerUnit (drawing unit → mm when the drawing has no DIMENSION), lineNoPattern (regex), rootHint [x,y] (drawing coords near the inlet), plan view: pipeLayers, headBlocks, headLayers, planHeightM; PDF: pages [1,2].

entry.description: zip only: entry name (or part of it) to show

ids.description: show: only these segment / node / run ids

component.description: show: only this connected component (0 = main network)

tools.name: spr_import_network
tools.description: Create the recognised (or a hand-written) pipe network in the sprinkler module in ONE undo step: nodes, pipes (nominal size, pipe standard, C, line number, valves), nozzles (kind closed|open|drain, K, required pressure, zone, line), drains and the water source. From a drawing: candidateId (+ components, excludeSegments/Nodes/Lines/Runs, source, defaults, drains, nozzleOverrides, zoneByLine/Run/Component, valves, placement). Hand-written: network = {version:1, units:"m", nodes:[{ref,x,y,z}], pipes:[{from,to,diameter,lineNo}], heads:[{node,kind,kFactor,requiredPressure,zone}], sources:[{node,sourceType,…}]}. Water-spray ISO nozzles default to open K80 (project default: general K80, zone deluge — confirm with the user). Validates first (nothing changes on error); dryRun only reports. scriptPath saves the payload JSON (re-import later). mode append (default) | replace. Then spr_run_calc.

network.description: Hand-written import payload (SprImportPayload) instead of candidateId

mode.description: append (default) adds to the current network; replace swaps it (design settings stay)

components.description: Connected components to import (default [0] = main network with the inlet)

excludeSegments.description: Candidate segment ids to drop (drain / air-blow / reference lines …)

source.description: Water source at candidate node (default = recognised inlet): sourceType pump|city_water|gravity_tank|pressure_tank, staticPressure, residualPressure, residualFlow, pumpRatedFlow, pumpRatedHead, pumpShutoffHead (MPa / L/min), tankElevation

defaults.description: kFactor (default 80), nozzleKind (default open for water spray), requiredPressure MPa, material (pipe standard id, e.g. JIS_G3454_STPG_SCH40), cFactor, stemDiameter (25), fallbackDiameter (50)

drains.description: Candidate nodes (open ends) that are drain holes — K or orifice diameter (default = nozzle K: drain hole = sprinkler orifice)

zoneByLine.description: { "<lineNo>": "<zone>" } — nozzles on that line get the zone (zone deluge scenarios)

valves.description: Valves on candidate segments: type, tag (WS-11U), zone (zone valve), open=false (closed)

placement.description: Place the drawing network: x,y,z offset of the inlet (m), rotateDeg about Z, mirrorY, floorIndex (story id; default by z)

scriptPath.description: Also save the import payload JSON to this path ("script" — can be re-imported with network=…)

dryRun.description: Only validate and report counts, change nothing

tools.name: spr_export_results
tools.description: Write the sprinkler / water-spray design results to files: format csv = 5 tables (summary, zones, lines by line number, nozzles, pipes; UTF-8 BOM), fhc = FHC (Canute) calculation-sheet style CSVs (report, heads, pipes, summary, lines, NFPA worksheet, node map), both. scenario = "all" | "zone:<zone>" (default governing scenario), at = supply (actual source) | design (inverse design point). zip=true also writes one zip per format. language = header language (ko default). Uses the current design results or recalculates them. fhcDraft=true adds the FHC project-file draft (.FHC) and pipe data table draft (.PDT) to the FHC files (check them in FHC before use). The FHC files include <name>_bulc_model.csv, which spr_import_fhc_bundle reads back exactly.

outputDir.description: Folder to write into (created if missing)

scenario.description: 'all' or 'zone:<zone>' (default: governing scenario of the design)

zip.description: Also write a zip per format

fhcDraft.description: fhc / both: also write the .FHC project draft + .PDT draft (default false)

slopeMode.description: .FHC draft sloping pipes: horizontal (default — length field = horizontal length), split (horizontal + U/D records), pipe (pipe length)

tools.name: spr_pump_sizing
tools.description: Pump specification for the sprinkler / water-spray network (deterministic). mode from_design (default): from the design calculation (per deluge zone or all-open) → rated flow and pressure with a safety margin, the points the pump curve must pass, NFPA 20 checks (churn ≤ 140 %, ≥ 65 % at 150 % flow), NFPA 20 standard capacity, hydraulic / shaft power and motor kW, NPSHa, pump type, governing zone and nozzle, governing-path losses and re-solved what-if hints (nozzle K −10 %, upsizing the bottleneck, closing drains, valve loss). mode target: a target flow and/or pressure at the source node. mode check_curve: check the network pump curve or a given curve. apply=true writes the proposed curve to the water source (then spr_run_calc).

targetPressureMPa.description: target: pressure at the network source node, MPa

curve.description: check_curve: curve points [{flow L/min, pressure MPa}] (default: the network pump source)

fluid.description: Sea water 1,025 kg/m³ for static heads (marine)

staticLiftM.description: Height of the network source node above the pump centreline, m (+ = pump below)

pumpPipeLossMPa.description: Extra pump → source-node loss at the max design flow, MPa

pumpPipe.description: Pump → source-node pipe {lengthM, diameterMm, material?, cFactor?, equivLengthM?}

suctionHeadM.description: Static suction head m (+ flooded, − lift)

strategy.description: Rated pressure: curve = cover all zone points with the assumed curve (default), envelope = max flow × max pressure

at150RatioPct.description: Assumed curve pressure at 150 % flow, % of rated (default 70)

apply.description: Write the proposed pump curve to the water source (one source)

tools.name: spr_design_review
tools.description: Specification and design-error review of the sprinkler / water-spray network and its design results (deterministic). Checks: pipe pressure rating by standard (KS D 3507 1.2 MPa NFTC 103, SGP, B31.1 wall formula, CuNi/GRE ratings), valve / flange class (JIS 5K/10K/16K/20K, PN, ASME class from valve std/tag), velocities vs limits, nozzles below required / above max pressure, imbalance, drains, closed valves isolating nozzles, disconnected / orphan / dead-end / coincident nodes, zero-length or duplicate pipes, expansion against flow, tee imbalance, high-loss valves, standards / sizes / C / K / required pressure data, zones and zone valves, stories and risers, pump curve NFPA 20 and run-out. Each finding: severity, category, location, message, suggested fix, ids.

category.description: spec = 사양 검토, design = 설계 오류 검토 (default all)

severity.description: List only this severity (e.g. warning — errors no longer fill the list)

code.description: List only this finding code (see byCode)

defaultFlangeClass.description: Class for valves / flanges without a marking

corrosionAllowanceMm.description: Wall corrosion allowance mm (default carbon steel 1.0)

limit.description: Findings to list (default: all when ≤ 100, else 40). byCode always summarises every code

tools.name: spr_import_fhc_bundle
tools.description: Load a BULC "FHC-style" export bundle back (zip, folder of CSVs, or *_bulc_model.csv). mode check (default) changes nothing: compares the bundle network and settings field by field with the CURRENT network, recalculates the bundle network and compares with the results written in the file (nozzle flows / pressures, required source pressure, summary). mode apply replaces the current pipe network with the bundle (undo history cleared, like opening a file) and runs the design calculation. Older bundles without bulc_model can only be partly restored (allowPartial). This is NOT an importer for files saved by the FHC (Canute) program.

allowPartial.description: apply: also load an older bundle without bulc_model (partial network)

recalc.description: apply: run the design calculation after loading (default true)

tools.name: hvac_get_results
tools.description: Get HVAC airflow calculation results (run hvac_run_calc first; any duct network edit clears them): total supply/exhaust flow (CFM and m³/s), supply − exhaust balance, duct velocity range and average (m/s), terminal flow range (CFM and m³/s). detail:true adds the result-dialog tables: per terminal design vs actual CFM (ok when actual ≥ 80 % of design) and per duct length, flow and velocity (ok < 10 m/s, warning ≤ 15, fail above).

detail.description: Include per-terminal and per-duct rows (default false)

tools.name: hvac_add_node
tools.description: Add an HVAC node (junction, supply_diffuser, exhaust_grille, or fan). Returns its id (give id to choose it, e.g. to reference it in hvac_add_duct / hvac_add_supply_diffuser in the same turn; default SUP_n / EXH_n / FAN_n / J_n). Equipment (diffuser, grille, air handler) is added with its own tool.

id.description: Optional node id (unique in the duct network)

z.description: Z position (m). Default: ceiling of the floorIndex story (zMin + height; the current story when floorIndex is omitted, 3.0 without stories) — same as the HVAC editor. hvac_apply_to_fds hangs the terminal box under that ceiling on the mesh grid

type.description: Node type: junction | supply_diffuser | exhaust_grille | fan

floorIndex.description: Story id (draw_list_stories id, 1 = first floor — same as spr_* and the HVAC editor, not 0-based). Default: the story that contains z (the current story when z is omitted)

tools.name: hvac_add_duct
tools.description: Connect two HVAC nodes with a duct (like drawing a duct in the HVAC editor: no duplicate or self-connection; roughness follows the material). Returns the duct id (optional id input, default D_n).

id.description: Optional duct id (unique in the duct network)

tools.name: hvac_add_supply_diffuser
