tools.description: Shape Studio: edit an existing feature/node (data) — everything downstream recomputes automatically (parametric). e.g. {id:"s3", params:{r:0.4}}, {params:{translate:[1,0,0]}} on a transform node, a fillet/chamfer {radius, edges:[{a,b,at?}] | edge_faces:[tags]} (refs are checked against the input body), a shell {thickness, open_faces}, an extrude {distance, mode}, an array {count, step}. Changing a field removes its parameter binding (use shape_bind for expressions).

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

params.description: Partial node params to merge (same keys as creation)

tools.name: shape_edit_node
tools.description: Shape Studio: rename / show-hide / suppress (feature stays in the history but is skipped; false = unsuppress) / assign FDS SURF / set color / mark axis fire faces + fire properties of a node. fire_faces: 6 booleans in FDS SURF_ID6 order [-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z] OR face names like ["-Z"] ("bottom"/"top" ok); [] clears. Fire properties merge (unspecified keep their value). ONE FIRE PER DEFINITION: assigning fire faces clears other nodes' and face-tag fire. PLAN FIRST: FDS fire only works on a FLAT face, so fire_faces without plan_confirmed changes nothing (fire_* in the same call are dropped) and returns a 6-direction flatness analysis — agree with the user on the flat face, HRRPUA, RAMP and combustion properties, then call again with plan_confirmed=true. For exact B-rep faces prefer shape_set_face.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

suppressed.description: true = suppress the feature (skipped in evaluation, later features use its input), false = unsuppress

fire_faces.description: [-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z] booleans or face names, [] to clear

fire_ramp_points.description: HRR time curve for RAMP_Q: [[t_seconds, fraction_0..1], ...]

fire_fuel_type.description: Fuel PRESET id — WOOD_OAK, POLYURETHANE_FOAM, COTTON, NYLON, POLYPROPYLENE, PVC, PMMA, GASOLINE (writes &REAC FUEL + chemistry). Other strings pass through as a raw FUEL name

plan_confirmed.description: Set true only AFTER the user agreed on the flat fire face and the fire properties (required to actually apply a fire face)

tools.name: shape_delete_node
tools.description: Shape Studio: delete a node. with_inputs (default true) also deletes its consumed input subtree (shared inputs are kept); with_inputs=false deletes only that feature and reconnects later features to its input.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_set_param
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: create / change / rename / remove a definition variable. expr is a number with units or an expression of other variables (mm cm m deg, + - * / ^, min max abs sqrt sin cos tan round floor ceil, pi). Bound node fields (shape_bind) and every placement recompute. Per-placement values: shape_set_instance param_overrides.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

name.description: Variable name (letter first; not a function/unit name)

tools.name: shape_bind
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: bind a node field to an expression of definition variables (or set a literal) — e.g. {node_id:'s1', field:'h', expr:'h'}, {field:'translate.2', expr:'clr + 0.1'}, {field:'points.2.0', expr:'w/2'}. A plain number sets the value and removes the binding; expr '' unbinds keeping the current value. Fields: w d h r r1 r2 tube height radius thickness distance count offset angleDeg translate.i rotateDeg.i scale.i step.i points.i.j …

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_set_face
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: set SURF and/or fire on B-rep faces chosen by tags, a selector (e.g. select {direction:'+Z', pick:'max'} = top face) or use_selection. surf_id '' clears. fire=true marks fire faces for the definition (one fire per definition; HRRPUA and fire_* go to the definition fire values); fire_* alone (no faces) just updates the fire values. PLAN FIRST: fire=true without plan_confirmed changes nothing and returns the chosen faces with planarity — agree with the user, then call again with plan_confirmed=true. Fire faces must be planar [rule:GEO-023]. Detached attributes (shape_get_tree detachedFaceAttrs — the face tag vanished after an edit): move_from=<old tag> + one target face re-picks them, tags=[old tag] + surf_id ''/fire false removes them. Without the kernel (no tags) an axis selector falls back to node axis fire faces.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

select.description: Face selector instead of guessing tags (build123d style): {direction:'+Z'|'-X'|…|[nx,ny,nz], pick:'max'(default, farthest along direction)|'min'|'all'|'largest'|'nearest', node:'s3' (faces made by this node or its inputs), point:[x,y,z] (for nearest), tol_deg:10, planar:true}

use_selection.description: true = use what the user selected in Shape Studio (the "Studio selection" line of the state) instead of passing tags/refs

surf_id.description: SURF id for these faces ('' clears)

move_from.description: Move the SURF/fire attributes of this (detached) face tag onto the single chosen face

fire_ramp_points.description: HRR time curve for RAMP_Q: [[t_seconds, fraction_0..1], ...]

fire_fuel_type.description: Fuel PRESET id — WOOD_OAK, POLYURETHANE_FOAM, COTTON, NYLON, POLYPROPYLENE, PVC, PMMA, GASOLINE (writes &REAC FUEL + chemistry). Other strings pass through as a raw FUEL name

plan_confirmed.description: Set true only AFTER the user agreed on the flat fire face and the fire properties (required to actually apply a fire face)

tools.name: shape_place
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: place a definition in the building — creates an instance (= one voxel obstacle with the same id, aligned to the MESH grid) at origin [x,y,z] (world m, where the definition origin goes), rotation_deg about z (CCW), optional storey_id (follows the storey floor height; origin z is then relative) and param_overrides {name: expr} for this placement only. Several placements share one definition.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

origin.description: World position of the definition origin (m)

storey_id.description: Storey id (draw_list_stories); origin z becomes relative to its floor

tools.name: shape_move_instance
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: move/rotate a placed shape (instance) rigidly. Relative: delta [dx,dy,dz] (m) and/or rotate_deg (CCW about z, around pivot [x,y] — default the instance origin). Absolute: origin [x,y,z] and/or rotation_deg. The derived voxel obstacle is rebuilt.

tools.name: shape_export_obst
tools.description: Shape Studio → FDS (compatibility): place or update an INSTANCE of the definition with id obstacle_id — the derived voxel obstacle follows the definition from then on (prefer shape_place / shape_move_instance). align_to_mesh (recommended) uses the MESH grid; voxel_size / cell set the definition voxel size; voxel_mode 'shell' voxelizes only the surface (hollow shapes); surf_id sets the definition SURF (these change the definition, i.e. all its placements). origin puts the bbox min corner at that world point (default: authored coordinates). node_id exports only that node's subtree as a new definition.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

obstacle_id.description: Instance / obstacle id (updated if it exists)

cell.description: Per-axis voxel size [dx,dy,dz] (m) — the definition uses one size (the smallest)

align_to_mesh.description: Use the (finest) project MESH cell size and grid origin

node_id.description: Export only this node (copied into a new definition)

origin.description: World position of the bbox min corner (default: authored coordinates)

surf_id.description: Definition SURF (default: node surf or INERT)

tools.name: shape_export_geom
tools.description: Shape Studio → FDS cut-cell: export the exact mesh of a definition (or node_id) as an &GEOM triangulated surface — no voxelization, so slopes and curves keep their true shape. Only a watertight surface is exported (the B-rep kernel gives closed booleans; an open mesh-fallback boolean is refused — voxelize those with shape_place/shape_export_obst). Needs a GPU engine build with cut-cell support. Fire (HRRPUA) on a GEOM surface is not supported yet. Units m, z-up, definition-local coordinates; origin repositions the bbox min corner.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

geom_id.description: New &GEOM ID (re-exporting with the same ID replaces it)

node_id.description: Node to export (default: every visible root, per-node SURF kept)

surf_id.description: SURF for all faces (default: per-node SURF, else FDS default surface)

origin.description: Domain position of bbox min corner (default: keep authored coords)

allow_open.description: Write the &GEOM even when the surface has holes (not recommended: FDS ERROR(730))

tools.name: shape_undo
tools.description: Shape Studio: undo (or redo=true) the last edits. With Shape Studio open: the studio working copy (one step per shape tool call / dialog). Otherwise in the app: the project history (Ctrl+Z — shape edits of one assistant round are one step); in headless MCP use project_undo. Applied after this round — call it alone, then re-read with shape_get_tree / shape_list.

tools.name: shape_new_document
tools.description: Shape Studio (legacy): with the Shape Studio session open, clear its working copy; otherwise start a new EMPTY shape definition in the project (same as shape_new_definition without a template). Later feature tools without def_id continue it.

tools.name: shape_duplicate_definition
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: copy a definition (features, variables, face attributes; not its placements) under a new id.

def_id.description: Definition to copy

tools.name: shape_remove_definition
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: delete a definition together with ALL its placements and their derived voxel obstacles.

tools.name: shape_set_definition
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: set definition properties — name, category, surf_id (default SURF of its obstacles, '' clears), fds_mode ('solid' fill | 'shell' surface only — use shell for walls thinner than a cell), cell (voxel size m; 0 = project MESH grid), ifc_class / ifc_object_type (IFC4 export). Affects every placement.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_set_rollback
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: roll the feature history back — evaluate only the first count features (later ones stay but are ignored; new features are inserted at that point). Or steps_back = how many features from the end to skip (2 = the last two). Features = feature-tree nodes in order (sketches are not counted). count -1 or both omitted = all.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

count.description: Features to evaluate from the start (-1 = all)

steps_back.description: Skip this many features from the end (alternative to count)

tools.name: shape_sketch
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: create or update a constrained 2D sketch (solved with the ezpz solver). plane 'XY'|'XZ'|'YZ' (+ offset along the plane axis), {origin, normal, x_axis}, or on_face = planar face tag (result gives its plane axes and face-centre uv; extrude adds/cuts that body); entities [{kind:'point',id,x,y} | {kind:'line',id,p1,p2} | {kind:'arc',id,center,start,end,ccw} | {kind:'circle',id,center,radius}] in plane coords (m); constraints [{type:'coincident'|'horizontal'|'vertical'|'parallel'|'perpendicular'|'tangent'|'equal'|'distance'|'hDistance'|'vDistance'|'length'|'radius'|'diameter'|'angle'|'symmetric'|'midpoint'|'pointOnLine'|'pointOnCircle'|'concentric'|'fix', a,b | line | curve | point, value (m/deg) or expr (definition variables)}]. Edit only dimensions: sketch_id + dimensions {constraint_id: value | 'expr'}. Returns solve status, DOF, conflicting/redundant constraints, closed profiles. Then shape_extrude_sketch.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

offset.description: Plane position along its axis (m) for XY/XZ/YZ

on_face.description: Planar face tag to sketch on, e.g. 's1:6' (sets the plane and host)

host_id.description: Node whose face the sketch sits on (extrude then adds/cuts it)

id.description: Optional constraint id (default c1, c2, … in order) — the result lists dimension ids; use them in dimensions

expr.description: Dimension expression of definition variables, e.g. 'w'

dimensions.description: Existing sketch: {constraint_id: number (m/deg) | expression string} — changes only those dimension values

tools.name: shape_set_instance
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: change a placement — param_overrides {name: expression | null to remove} (this placement only), clear_overrides, hidden (true removes its obstacle without deleting the placement), storey_id (-1 = none), rename_to (also renames the obstacle).

tools.name: shape_remove_instance
tools.description: Shape Studio v2: delete placements (and their derived voxel obstacles). The definitions stay.

tools.name: shape_hull
tools.description: Shape Studio: convex hull of the given nodes (blob/rounded forms). Mesh kernel only — no face tags, cannot be filleted/shelled.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_import_mesh
tools.description: Shape Studio: import an STL or OBJ file as a mesh node (metres) into a definition. y_up=true if the file is Y-up (converted to Z-up). Mesh-only (no face tags, no fillet/shell). For GLB/FBX use the Shape Studio UI import button.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_export_stl
tools.description: Shape Studio → CFD (OpenFOAM etc.): export the exact mesh of a definition (B-rep kernel triangulation when available) as STL (no voxelization). ascii=true for text STL with solid name (snappyHexMesh patch name). Units m, z-up, definition-local coordinates.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_export_obj
tools.description: Shape Studio → CFD: export the exact mesh of a definition as OBJ (no voxelization). Units m, z-up, definition-local coordinates.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

tools.name: shape_register_item
tools.description: Shape Studio: voxelize a definition (or node_id) and register it as a reusable library item (furniture/item catalog). It then appears in the app's Item panel and is placed from there (place_furniture only knows the built-in catalog). combustible / hrrpua / material are stored on the item, but that alone does not make it burn — set the FDS fire preset with shape_set_item_fds_props.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

node_id.description: Node to register (default: the whole definition)

tools.name: shape_set_item_fds_props
tools.description: Item library: set FDS fire/material properties on a registered item (shown via the item panel's 'Library FDS Properties' button and applied when the item is placed). Sets a 'fire' preset override.

tools.name: shape_get_item_fds_props
tools.description: Item library: read the FDS properties and metadata of a registered item.

tools.name: shape_screenshot
tools.description: Shape Studio: capture a screenshot of the running GUI (Shape Studio opens automatically) so you can visually REVIEW the shape you built. Returns a PNG file path — read the image, compare against reference photos, then fix with shape_set_params. select_node opens that node in the property panel first (e.g. to review fire faces / HRR chart). Live GUI mode only.

select_node.description: Node id to select before capture (shows its property panel)

tools.name: shape_preview_voxels
tools.description: Shape Studio: switch the Shape Studio viewport into FDS voxel preview — shows exactly what the shape becomes as FDS OBST boxes (incl. fire faces). By default it uses the project MESH grid (cell size AND grid origin, so the preview matches the derived obstacle); size (m) only applies when there is no mesh or align_to_mesh=false. mode 'solid'|'shell'. off=true returns to the smooth view. GUI only (no effect headless).

size.description: Voxel edge (m) when not aligned to the mesh (default 0.1)

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Read the open project: file path, unsaved changes, CHID, deck path used for runs, stories (id, name, zMin, height, EVAC floorIndex), domain and mesh cells, object counts per module. Call this first in a session and after project_open. Read-only.

tools.name: project_open
tools.description: Open a .bulc project or a .fds deck in the running BULC app (same as File > Open, including evacuation, drawing, sprinkler and HVAC side files). path must be absolute. Refuses when the open project has unsaved changes unless discard_unsaved=true (ask the user first). Live app only.

path.description: Absolute path of a .bulc or .fds file

discard_unsaved.description: Discard unsaved changes of the current project (default false)

tools.name: project_save
tools.description: Save the open project as a .bulc bundle (.bulc + .fds + _evac.json + _spr.json + _hvac.json) like File > Save. Without path it saves to the current .bulc file. A new path must end with .bulc; an existing file is only replaced with overwrite=true. Saving renames CHID to the file name (GEN-009) — result files follow it. Live app only.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at a new path (default false)

tools.name: project_new
tools.description: Start a new empty project in the running app (File > New): clears geometry, evacuation, sprinkler, HVAC and drawing state. Refuses when there are unsaved changes unless discard_unsaved=true. Live app only.

tools.name: project_export_fds
tools.description: Write the current model as an FDS 6.10.1 input deck (.fds) to path (absolute, must end with .fds). CHID becomes the file name. Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite=true. To only read the deck use preview_fds. Live app only.

tools.name: project_undo
tools.description: Undo the last model edit(s) of the fire model (obstacles, holes, vents, devices, settings …) like Ctrl+Z. steps 1–20 (default 1). Sprinkler/HVAC/evacuation module edits have their own tools.

tools.name: project_redo
tools.description: Redo model edits undone with project_undo (Ctrl+Y). steps 1–20 (default 1).

tools.name: get_conventions
tools.description: Units, coordinate axes, story / floorIndex numbering, id rules and file conventions used by the BULC tools (they differ between modules — read this before building a model from a drawing). topic = units | coordinates | floors | ids | files | aset | all (default all). Read-only.

tools.name: fds_apply_text
tools.description: Apply an edited FDS deck to the project: send the complete .fds text (start from preview_fds, edit, send back). The deck is parsed and compared section by section with the current model; only changed sections (meshes, obstacles, vents, devices, controls, dump …) are applied, untouched sections keep their app metadata (changed sections are replaced by the parsed values). dryRun (default true) only reports the changed sections. sections limits which top-level sections may change. Nothing changes on a parse error.

tools.name: sim_preflight
tools.description: Pre-run check with structured results: every issue carries a knowledge-pack rule id (e.g. OUT-001, VENT-001, MESH-002). Combines validate_project, the run dialog deck checks (output intervals ≥ T_END, deck reference errors CPU FDS rejects, fires outside the mesh, spray keys the chosen GPU solver ignores, LOCK_TIME_STEP stability hint) and grid resolution advice (D*/dx from the peak HRR). ok=false means do not run. solver = gpu (default) | gpu_cutcell | cpu_openmp. Read-only.

tools.name: sim_start
tools.description: Start the fire simulation in the running app after the user agreed (confirm=true required). Runs sim_preflight first and refuses on errors (force=true only if the user explicitly accepts). The deck is written next to the saved project (.bulc → .fds, like the toolbar RUN) or, for an unsaved project, to Documents/bulc_<folder>/. Refuses while another run is active. solver = gpu (default) | gpu_cutcell | cpu_openmp; restart=true resumes from the checkpoint. Then poll sim_status. Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

location.description: project (default when the project is saved) | documents

restart.description: Resume from the restart checkpoint (default false)

force.description: Start even if sim_preflight reports errors (default false)

tools.name: sim_status
tools.description: Status of the current / last fire simulation of this app session: running or finished, exit code, simulated time vs T_END (percent, ETA), step, dt, CFL, HRR (kW), Tmax (K), max velocity, NaN count, health flags (nan=0, Tmax ≤ 2500 K, |u| < 50 m/s) and sprinkler / detector activation times read from the engine log. Read-only.

tools.name: sim_stop
tools.description: Stop the running fire simulation (confirm=true). mode graceful (default) writes <CHID>.stop so the engine finishes its output files and a restart checkpoint; mode kill ends the process at once (results may be incomplete). Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

tools.name: sim_log_tail
tools.description: Last lines of the engine console output of the current / last run (lines ≤ 500, default 60). grep = optional regular expression filter. Read-only.

grep.description: Only lines matching this regular expression (case-insensitive)

tools.name: results_detect
tools.description: Find the result files of a deck (named by its &HEAD CHID, next to the .fds): .smv, _hrr.csv, _devc.csv, _ctrl.csv, .out, and list the slice planes (quantity + plane), Plot3D times / quantities, Smoke3D, boundary and particle files. Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: fire_results_summary
tools.description: Summarise a finished (or running) fire simulation from its result files: peak HRR and time, total heat released (MJ), radiative fraction, last simulated time vs T_END, every device column (max, time of max, final, unit), first time each device with a setpoint reached it, sprinkler / detector activation times from the engine log of this session, and the available output files. Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: fire_timeseries
tools.description: Time series from the result CSV files: file = hrr (HRR, Q_RADI, MLR …) | devc (device ids) | ctrl. columns = column names (default the first 6). t0 / t1 limit the time window; maxPoints ≤ 500 (default 300 — longer series are reduced by time-averaging). Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: fire_compute_aset
tools.description: Available safe egress time (ASET) at breathing height: for each point (default: every user exit — OPEN vents, door items, Door_/Window_ holes) the time series at floor + samplingHeight (default 1.8 m) is read from horizontal slices (preferred) or Plot3D and compared with the criteria (default temperature 60 °C, visibility 5 m, CO 1,400 ppm, O2 15 %, CO2 5 %; same as the app ASET report). Returns ASET per point, the governing criterion, a lower bound when no criterion is exceeded, and which quantities are missing (then add output_add_tenability_slices and re-run). points[].floorZ = floor elevation of that point (or story = story id). Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

source.description: Data source (default auto: slices, then Plot3D)

tools.name: output_add_tenability_slices
tools.description: Add the horizontal slices the ASET check needs at floor + height (default 1.8 m) on every story (or the given story ids / absolute z): TEMPERATURE, VISIBILITY and VOLUME FRACTION of OXYGEN, CARBON DIOXIDE, CARBON MONOXIDE (quantities can be limited). Existing identical slices are skipped. Run before sim_start (OUT-006, ASET-004).

z.description: Absolute plane heights instead of stories

height.description: Height above each story floor (default 1.8 m)

tools.name: capture_view
tools.description: Screenshot of the running app for visual checking: view = current (default) | 2d (plan of a story) | 3d | result (result viewer) | shape (Shape Studio). story = story id to show in 2D. region = viewport (default, only the drawing area) | window. Returns the PNG as an image (and its path); savePath (absolute .png) also keeps a copy. Live app only.

maxWidth.description: Downscale to this width in pixels (default 1600)

savePath.description: Also save the PNG here (absolute .png path)

tools.name: evac_run
tools.description: Run the evacuation simulation in the running app after the user agreed (confirm=true): builds the same engine input as the EVAC run dialog (agents, exits = OPEN vents / door items / Door_·Window_ holes, walls, stairs → multi-level mode, waypoints, journeys, FED and alarm settings) and starts the engine in the background. Refuses with no agents, and with no user-defined exits unless allowNoExits=true (the engine would then use temporary exits at the domain edges). Poll evac_status, then read evac_get_results. Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

outputFolder.description: Folder for the .evac result file (default: the project folder)

allowNoExits.description: Run even without user-defined exits (default false)

tools.name: evac_status
tools.description: Status of the current / last evacuation run of this app session: running or finished, percent, last engine message, error, result summary. Read-only.

tools.name: evac_stop
tools.description: Stop the running evacuation simulation (confirm=true). No result is kept. Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

tools.name: evac_get_results
tools.description: Summary of the last evacuation result in the project (never the raw trajectories): agents, evacuated / remaining, last exit time (the RSET shown in the app), mean and p50/p90/p95 exit times, evacuation start delay from the alarm chain, FED casualties and their causes, per-exit counts, first/last times and flow (persons/s/m; each agent is assigned to the exit nearest to its last position), stair and evacuation-elevator statistics, per-floor results and whether the agents changed since the run (stale). detail = summary (default) | exits | agents (agents lists exit times, limit ≤ 500). aset_s (e.g. from fire_compute_aset) adds the design check RSET = pre-movement + movement × (1 + safetyFactor) vs ASET, as in the app ASET/RSET report; rset overrides detection / alarm / pre-movement times (s, defaults 30 / 3 / 60, or the alarm-chain start the run used) and safetyFactor (default 0.15). Read-only.

aset_s.description: ASET (s) to compare with the design RSET

tools.name: arch_analyze_drawing
tools.description: Read an architectural floor plan (.dxf, .dwg via the bundled converter, vector .pdf, or an image) and recognise the building: units and scale (DXF $INSUNITS, dimension values, PDF scale text), layer roles, wall centrelines with thickness (double-line or single-line walls), doors (swing arcs / door blocks), windows (window layers / blocks), columns, stair areas, room names and story labels. Returns candidateId, a summary and questions to confirm with the user (DRW-001…003). Images and outlined PDFs return needsVision — then read the picture yourself and call arch_import_floorplan_report. show = walls | openings | columns | rooms | levels | layers lists details (offset, limit, ids). Read-only; the file is read on this PC only.

candidateId.description: Re-use an earlier analysis (with options = analyse again)

options.description: Re-analysis options: scaleMmPerUnit (drawing unit → mm; PDF: scale denominator, 1:100 → 100), wallLayers / doorLayers / windowLayers / columnLayers / excludeLayers (layer names), wallStyle auto|double|single, wallThicknessRange [min,max] m (default [0.05,0.6]), defaultWallThickness m (single-line walls, default 0.2), minWallLength m (default 0.3), page (PDF page, default 1).

tools.name: arch_import_building
tools.description: Create the building on one story in ONE undo step: walls as obstacles (axis-aligned box per wall, diagonal walls stair-stepped like the 2D editor), doors as holes 'Door_<prefix>n' (also evacuation exits) and windows as holes 'Win_<prefix>n' at sill height (not exits), optional columns and slabs. Source: candidateId from arch_analyze_drawing (exclude walls / openings by id) or building = {walls:[{start:[x,y],end:[x,y],thickness?,height?}], doors:[{at:[x,y]|wall:n,position:0..1,width?,height?}], windows:[{at|wall,position,width?,sill?,height?}], columns:[{xb:[x1,x2,y1,y2]}|{center,size}]} in metres; wall:n counts from 1 in the order of building.walls (openings that cannot be placed are listed in warnings). story = story id (default current story; z = its zMin, wall height = its height). dryRun defaults to TRUE — report first, confirm with the user, then call again with dryRun:false. mode append (default) | replace (removes what an earlier import with the same idPrefix created).

building.description: Hand-written building spec (metres) instead of candidateId. Door/window wall:n is 1-based (wall 1 = building.walls[0])

zBase.description: Floor elevation instead of the story zMin (m)

transform.description: Placement: origin = 'bbox_min' (default for drawings: lower-left corner of the building) | 'none' | [x,y] in drawing metres; target [x,y] (default [0,0]); rotateDeg about the target (counter-clockwise); mirrorY. Use the same origin for every story drawing of one building.

defaults.description: wallHeight (default: story height), wallThickness (walls without one, default 0.2), doorWidth 0.9, doorHeight 2.1, windowWidth 1.2, windowSill 0.9, windowHeight 1.2, slabThickness 0.2 (m)

include.description: What to create: doors (true), windows (true), columns (true), floorSlab (false — slab just below the story floor), ceilingSlab (false — slab on top of the walls)

maxObstacles.description: Refuse above this many obstacles (default 3000, max 20000)

tools.name: arch_import_floorplan_report
tools.description: Build walls / doors / windows from YOUR reading of a floor-plan picture (image or outlined PDF page — use when arch_analyze_drawing says needsVision). report = {building_width_m (real width of the outer walls), wall_height_m?, wall_thickness_m?, walls:[{x1,y1,x2,y2}] wall CENTRELINES in normalised image coordinates 0..1 (origin top-left, y down; split at corners, skip dimension lines, text, furniture, hatching), doors:[{x,y,width_m?}], windows:[{x,y,width_m?,sill_m?,height_m?}]}. image = {width,height} pixels (or imagePath) for the aspect ratio. The app converts the report with fixed rules (snap to horizontal/vertical, y flipped, origin at the lower-left wall corner) and creates the same objects as arch_import_building (BIM walls / doors / windows in a BIM floor-plan project). Needs no AI key in the app. dryRun defaults to TRUE.

imagePath.description: Absolute path of the image (its header gives the size)

transform.description: Placement: origin = 'bbox_min' (default for drawings: lower-left corner of the building) | 'none' | [x,y] in drawing metres; target [x,y] (default [0,0]); rotateDeg about the target (counter-clockwise); mirrorY. Use the same origin for every story drawing of one building.

defaults.description: wallHeight (default: story height), wallThickness (walls without one, default 0.2), doorWidth 0.9, doorHeight 2.1, windowWidth 1.2, windowSill 0.9, windowHeight 1.2, slabThickness 0.2 (m)

include.description: What to create: doors (true), windows (true), columns (true), floorSlab (false — slab just below the story floor), ceilingSlab (false — slab on top of the walls)

tools.name: bim_add_stair
tools.description: Add a BIM stair (IfcStair) from storey_id to top_storey_id (story ids, 1F = 1; default top = the story above) in one undo step, like the floor-plan stair tool: treads and landings as stepped OBST plates, slab holes in the upper floors and, with enclosure (default true), stair-shaft walls with one door per story (owned BIM walls/doors). kind normal | escape (default) | special (adds a vestibule in front of the shaft door on every story; pressurized → supply vent, supply_flow_m3s). shape u (default: two flights + mid landing, repeated every story) | straight (one flight, one story). Place with x,y = inner-box corner (local origin; local +x = first flight climbing direction, the shaft door is in the local x=0 wall) or center = [x,y]; rotation 0/90/180/270. The riser is refitted to each story height. It becomes an evacuation stair automatically. Returns the id, risers per story, inner-box size and owned object ids.

top_storey_id.description: Top story id (default: the story above storey_id). A straight stair spans one story only

x.description: Origin x = inner-box corner (m); give with y

center.description: Alternative to x,y: centre [x,y] of the inner box (m)

rotation.description: Plan rotation in degrees CCW (default 0). Any angle; 0/90/180/270 give exact grid-aligned FDS boxes, other angles become diagonal walls and rasterized treads

shape.description: u (default): two flights + mid landing | straight: one flight

riser.description: Target riser (m, default 0.18; refitted to each story height)

gap.description: Gap between the two U flights (m, default 0.2)

enclosure.description: Build the stair-shaft walls and doors (default true)

door_width.description: Shaft door width per story (m, default 1.0)

width.description: Along the door face (m, default 2.4; elevator lobby 3)

depth.description: Outward from the door face (m, default 2.0)

pressurized.description: Supply vent on every story (default true)

supply_flow_m3s.description: Supply air per story (m³/s, default 0.8) → MASS_FLUX vent

vestibule.description: kind 'special' only (U shape): vestibule in front of the shaft door

capacity.description: Persons on the stair at once (default EVAC 5)

speed.description: Walking speed on the stair (m/s, default EVAC 0.6)

evac.description: Evacuation values of the derived evacuation stair

tools.name: bim_add_elevator
tools.description: Add a BIM elevator (IfcTransportElement ELEVATOR) from storey_id to top_storey_id (story ids; default top = the highest story) in one undo step: shaft walls on every story, a landing door per story in the local y=0 wall and slab holes for the shaft (the car is not an FDS object). Optional lobby = landing vestibule (walls + corridor door; pressurized → supply vent). kind passenger | emergency (default) | evacuation. Place with x,y = inner shaft corner (local origin) or center = [x,y]; rotation 0/90/180/270. evac = evacuation operation (enabled default true, capacity persons, speed m/s, accel m/s², door_open/door_close s, board_time s per person, start_delay s, discharge_storey_id default = the ground story of the span). Returns the id, one-way travel time t = d/v + v/a (or 2√(d/a) on short runs) and the full-car round trip 2t + 2(door_open + door_close) + 2·capacity·board_time.

top_storey_id.description: Top story id (default: the highest story)

x.description: Origin x = inner-box corner (m); give with y

center.description: Alternative to x,y: centre [x,y] of the inner box (m)

rotation.description: Plan rotation in degrees CCW (default 0). Any angle; 0/90/180/270 give exact grid-aligned FDS boxes, other angles become diagonal walls and rasterized treads

shaft_width.description: Inner shaft width along the door face (m, default 2.4)

width.description: Along the door face (m, default 2.4; elevator lobby 3)

depth.description: Outward from the door face (m, default 2.0)

pressurized.description: Supply vent on every story (default true)

supply_flow_m3s.description: Supply air per story (m³/s, default 0.8) → MASS_FLUX vent

discharge_storey_id.description: Discharge story id (default: the ground story of the span)

tools.name: bim_update_stair
tools.description: Change a BIM stair by id (Stair_N, see bim_list_vertical) — give only the fields to change (same meaning as bim_add_stair). Its shaft walls, doors, treads, slab holes and vestibule are rebuilt; owned walls and doors keep their ids, door states and leakage. x,y or center moves it; without them the origin corner stays where it is (a larger stair grows away from that corner). vestibule and evac fields merge with the current values.

top_storey_id.description: Top story id (default: the story above storey_id). A straight stair spans one story only

x.description: Origin x = inner-box corner (m); give with y

center.description: Alternative to x,y: centre [x,y] of the inner box (m)

rotation.description: Plan rotation in degrees CCW (default 0). Any angle; 0/90/180/270 give exact grid-aligned FDS boxes, other angles become diagonal walls and rasterized treads

shape.description: u (default): two flights + mid landing | straight: one flight

riser.description: Target riser (m, default 0.18; refitted to each story height)

gap.description: Gap between the two U flights (m, default 0.2)

enclosure.description: Build the stair-shaft walls and doors (default true)

door_width.description: Shaft door width per story (m, default 1.0)

width.description: Along the door face (m, default 2.4; elevator lobby 3)

depth.description: Outward from the door face (m, default 2.0)

pressurized.description: Supply vent on every story (default true)

supply_flow_m3s.description: Supply air per story (m³/s, default 0.8) → MASS_FLUX vent

vestibule.description: kind 'special' only (U shape): vestibule in front of the shaft door

capacity.description: Persons on the stair at once (default EVAC 5)

speed.description: Walking speed on the stair (m/s, default EVAC 0.6)

evac.description: Evacuation values of the derived evacuation stair

tools.name: bim_update_elevator
tools.description: Change a BIM elevator by id (Elevator_N, see bim_list_vertical) — give only the fields to change (same meaning as bim_add_elevator). Shaft walls, landing doors, slab holes and lobby are rebuilt; owned walls and doors keep their ids, door states and leakage. x,y or center moves it (otherwise the origin corner stays). lobby {enabled:false} removes the lobby; lobby and evac fields merge with the current values. Returns the new travel and round-trip times.

top_storey_id.description: Top story id (default: the highest story)

x.description: Origin x = inner-box corner (m); give with y

center.description: Alternative to x,y: centre [x,y] of the inner box (m)

rotation.description: Plan rotation in degrees CCW (default 0). Any angle; 0/90/180/270 give exact grid-aligned FDS boxes, other angles become diagonal walls and rasterized treads

shaft_width.description: Inner shaft width along the door face (m, default 2.4)

width.description: Along the door face (m, default 2.4; elevator lobby 3)

depth.description: Outward from the door face (m, default 2.0)

pressurized.description: Supply vent on every story (default true)

supply_flow_m3s.description: Supply air per story (m³/s, default 0.8) → MASS_FLUX vent

discharge_storey_id.description: Discharge story id (default: the ground story of the span)

tools.name: bim_list_vertical
tools.description: List the BIM stairs and elevators (read-only): id, kind, shape, storeys, origin, rotation, inner-box / shaft footprint, risers per story or elevator travel and round-trip times, and the ids of the walls, doors, treads, slab holes and supply vents each one owns. Owned objects are rebuilt from the element — change them with bim_update_stair / bim_update_elevator; removing one of them (remove_obstacle / remove_hole) removes the whole stair or elevator. id = only that element.

tools.name: bim_remove_vertical
tools.description: Remove a BIM stair or elevator by id (an id of one of its owned walls or doors also works) together with its shaft walls, doors, treads, slab holes, vestibule / lobby and supply vents, in one undo step. Evacuation stairs and elevators derived from it disappear too.

id.description: Stair_N / Elevator_N (or an owned wall / door id)

tools.name: hvac_fds_namelist
tools.description: Edit the FDS &HVAC duct network kept as raw deck lines (imported from a deck or made here; the HVAC module's own duct network is never written as &HVAC), like the 'FDS &HVAC edit' dialog. action list (default) | add | update | rename | remove. add: type_id DUCT | NODE | FAN | FILTER | AIRCOIL | LEAK, optional id (default <TYPE>_n) and keys; update: id + keys {KEY: value, null deletes}; strings are quoted unless already quoted, numeric or logical, arrays become lists (e.g. {NODE_ID:['N1','N2'], AREA:0.04, LOSS:[1,1], VOLUME_FLOW:0.5, N_CELLS:10}); rename: id + new_id (also renames &HVAC references and device DUCT_ID / NODE_ID); remove: id (references are reported). cell_l sets &MISC HVAC_MASS_TRANSPORT_CELL_L [m] (null clears). A node VENT_ID needs an &VENT with SURF_ID='HVAC'. Returns the lines and checks (ERROR 524/551/518, missing references, one-duct node without vent).

id.description: &HVAC ID (add: optional; update / rename / remove: required)

keys.description: add / update: &HVAC keys to set (KEY: value; null deletes the key)

tools.name: bim_import_ifc
tools.description: Import an IFC file (IFC4 or IFC2X3 STEP, .ifc) into the BIM floor plan: storeys, walls, doors, windows, openings, slabs, spaces, stairs and elevators, plus proxies/furniture as Shape Studio shapes; derived FDS obstacles/holes/voxels in the same undo step. Wall/slab material layers → layered SURF/MATL (IFC thermal values, else library by name, ≤4 layers), never overwriting same-id ones. mode=replace swaps the BIM elements and storey list (File menu rule; shapes merged, same GlobalId replaced in place). mode=merge keeps the current model: IFC storeys join existing ones at the same elevation (±0.05 m) or become new storeys, elements with the same GlobalId are replaced in place and clashing ids are renamed. storey_filter = IFC storey names or ids to import. dry_run=true only reads and reports (per-class counts, unit, approximations incl. materials, skipped #ids, FDS counts, extent vs mesh) — call it first and confirm replace with the user. path: absolute or relative to the project folder; must end with .ifc.

path.description: IFC file path (.ifc) — absolute, or relative to the project folder

mode.description: replace = swap the BIM model and storeys; merge = add to the current model

storey_filter.description: IFC storey names or ids to import (default: all) — see dry_run

include_shapes.description: Import IfcBuildingElementProxy / IfcFurniture as shapes (default true)

dry_run.description: Read and report only, change nothing (default false)

tools.name: bim_export_ifc
tools.description: Write the BIM floor plan to an IFC4 STEP file: storeys, walls, doors, windows, openings, slabs, spaces, stairs and elevators (SURF_ID, door state and leakage in BULC property sets, restored when read back; layered SURFs as IfcMaterialLayerSet with MATL thermal properties), and with include_shapes (default true) the Shape Studio placements. path: absolute or relative to the project folder, must end with .ifc, the folder must exist; an existing file is replaced only with overwrite=true (atomic write of that one file, no backup or other files). project_name = IfcProject name (default CHID). Returns the per-class counts written and warnings. Check the file with bim_import_ifc {dry_run:true}.

path.description: Output .ifc path — absolute, or relative to the project folder

include_shapes.description: Also write Shape Studio placements (default true)

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (default false — ask the user first)

tools.name: bim_get_model
tools.description: List the BIM model (read-only), each item with its id: storeys (floor elevation, height, element counts), walls (end points a/b, length, thickness, height, base offset, SURF, owner stair/elevator), openings (door / window / opening, host wall, offset along the wall, width, height, sill), slabs (kind, extent, area, thickness, top offset, holes), spaces (name, area, extent), stairs, elevators and Shape Studio placements. Heights are relative to the storey floor. storey_id = one storey; kinds = which lists; ids = only these elements; limit = rows per list (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: bim_derive_fds
tools.description: Show how the BIM model becomes FDS input (deterministic): derived obstacles (wall pieces, slabs, stair treads), holes (doors, windows, openings, slab and shaft holes) and supply vents, with the approximations — diagonal walls (and walls mitred to them) as footprint polygons rasterised to the mesh grid when the deck is written (cell-centre rule plus a centre-line cell chain so sub-cell walls leave no gap; doors cut them into pieces with PERMIT_HOLE guards), non-rectangular slabs and rotated treads rasterised the same way, Shape Studio placements voxelised at the mesh cell. Also checks drift between the BIM model and the derived objects in the project (missing, stale, moved). element_ids = derived ids and XB of these elements; storey_id = limit the approximation list to one storey. regenerate=true rebuilds every derived object from the BIM model (one undo step) — use it when drift is reported.

storey_id.description: Story id — approximations for this storey only

element_ids.description: BIM element ids (Wall_3, Door_1, Floor_2, Stair_1 …) or shape placement ids

regenerate.description: Rebuild all derived obstacles / holes / vents from the BIM model (default false)

tools.name: list_expert_keys
tools.description: List FDS 6.11.1 global expert keys from the catalog (groups TIME, MISC, RADI, PRES, COMB, WIND, CLIP, DUMP): key, type/unit, FDS default, valid range or choices, GPU engine support (read / partial / IGNORED = CPU FDS only) and a one-line description. Filter by group, query (part of a key or description, Korean or English) and gpu. Without group and query it returns a per-group summary. Test/diagnostic keys are hidden unless include_debug. Read-only — set values with set_expert_settings.

query.description: Substring of a key or description, e.g. "SMAGORINSKY", "radiation", "압력"

gpu.description: Only keys with this GPU engine support

tools.name: get_expert_settings
tools.description: Read the explicit expert settings per FDS group (TIME, MISC, RADI, PRES, COMB, WIND, CLIP, DUMP): every key the generated deck writes, with value, FDS default, unit, GPU engine support and where the GUI keeps it (structured field such as numerics / particle_global / dump, the &TIME/&MISC/&DUMP extra keys, or the single raw &GROUP line). Keys outside the FDS 6.11.1 catalog are flagged. Omit group for all groups. Keys not listed run at the FDS default. Read-only.

tools.name: set_expert_settings
tools.description: Set or remove FDS 6.11.1 global expert keys of one group (TIME, MISC, RADI, PRES, COMB, WIND, CLIP, DUMP), validated against the catalog: type, range, choices, array length and cross-key rules (LOCK_TIME_STEP needs DT, CFL_MIN < CFL_MAX, GEOSTROPHIC_WIND needs LATITUDE, one radiation absorption model, DNS has no TURBULENCE_MODEL …). set = {KEY: value} (number, true/false, string, array); unset = [KEY] returns keys to the FDS default. Values go where the dialogs, set_numerics and set_ambient keep them (structured fields first, else the single &GROUP line — never a duplicate line). All-or-nothing: any error changes nothing. The result warns when the GPU engine ignores a key (CPU FDS only). Discover keys with list_expert_keys.

unset.description: Keys to remove (back to the FDS default)

tools.name: shape_get_edges
tools.description: Shape Studio: list the B-rep edges of a body for edge-selective shape_add_fillet / shape_add_chamfer. Edge ref = the two adjacent face tags {a, b} (sorted), plus at=[x,y,z] (definition-local m, chain midpoint) only when several edges join the same two faces (siblings > 1). Rows: ref, faces [a,b], length_m, mid, siblings. node = a node id — its own body even if a later feature consumed it (use the fillet's input); default every visible root. faces = only edges touching these face tags. Pass ref objects unchanged as edges. Mesh-only results (no kernel, hull/imported mesh) have no edges.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

node.description: Node id whose body to list (default: every visible root)

faces.description: Only edges touching these face tags, e.g. ['s1:6']

tools.name: shape_measure
tools.description: Shape Studio (Inspect · Measure): exact measurements from the shape kernel. No targets = every visible body (volume, surface area, bounding box) and the total. One target = its values (body volume/area/bbox, face area/normal/centre, edge length/direction, point). Two targets = both plus the distance (point–point with ΔXYZ, point–plane, plane–plane for parallel faces, edge–edge minimum) and the angle between face normals / straight edges. use_selection measures what the user selected in Shape Studio. Definition-local metres.

def_id.description: Target shape definition id (ShapeDef_n, see shape_list). Default: the definition open in the Shape Studio session, else the one you last edited, else the only one (feature tools create a new definition when none applies)

items.description: One pick: {node:'s3'} = that node's body (its own body even if consumed later) | {face:'s1:6'} | {edge:{a,b,at?}} | {point:[x,y,z]} (definition-local m)

edge.description: Edge reference: the two adjacent face tags (any order) and, only when several edges join the same two faces, at=[x,y,z] (definition-local m) picking the nearest one

targets.description: Up to two picks (omit = whole definition)

use_selection.description: true = use what the user selected in Shape Studio (the "Studio selection" line of the state) instead of passing tags/refs

tools.name: shape_studio
tools.description: Shape Studio window (app only): action 'open' opens the studio on def_id / instance_id (edit that placement's definition) / template (new definition from a template) / nothing (new empty definition) — later shape tools without def_id then edit it live; 'commit' = the 완료 button: saves the studio working copy into the project (config.shapes, one project undo step, re-derives the placements' obstacles) and closes the studio — a new definition is not placed yet (shape_place); 'cancel' = discard the unsaved studio edits and close (only when the user asks). Only one studio session at a time.

def_id.description: open: definition to edit (shape_list)

instance_id.description: open: placement whose definition to edit

template.description: open: start a new definition from this template

tools.name: view_get_state
tools.description: Read the current model view (display only): 2D plan or 3D, the story shown in the 2D plan (story id), the 3D render mode, which display layers are on with their element counts (IFC-imported walls, doors, windows, slabs, structure, stairs, finishes, furniture, sprinkler, HVAC, piping, electrical, equipment), mesh outline / OPEN boundary visibility, the objects hidden one by one and the 3D smoke preview (on/off, playing, quality, speed, density). Change it with view_set_layers / view_set; count elements with view_count_elements.

tools.name: view_set_layers
tools.description: Show or hide parts of the model view by display layer — e.g. "show only sprinklers" {only:["sprinkler"]}, "hide piping" {hide:["pipe"]}, "walls, doors and windows only" {preset:"default"}, "show everything" {preset:"all"}. Layers: wall, door, window, slab, structure, stair, finish, furniture, sprinkler, hvac, pipe, electrical, equipment, other; groups mep / architecture; Korean names work too (스프링클러, 공조, 덕트, 배관, 벽, 문, 창, 바닥, 지붕, 기둥, 보, 계단, 마감, 천장, 가구, 전기, 조명, 설비기기). Applied in order preset → only → show / hide. Also mesh (mesh outline), openBoundaries (OPEN boundary faces), unhideObjects (objects hidden one by one) and colorByLayer ("color by type": 3D colors per layer — sprinkler red, ducts cyan, pipes green, electrical yellow; false = surface colors). Display only: hidden layers stay in the FDS deck. Layers exist for IFC-imported elements; objects without a layer (drawn, read from .fds) always show. Returns the new visibility with counts.

preset.description: default = walls, doors, windows only; all = every layer; none = no layer

only.description: Show only these layers (all others hidden)

unhideObjects.description: true = show again the objects hidden one by one (3D right-click Hide)

colorByLayer.description: true = color IFC elements by layer in 3D (layer bar "Colors"); false = surface (SURF) colors

tools.name: view_set
tools.description: Change how the model is viewed (display only, the FDS deck is not changed): view = 2d (floor plan) | 3d; story = story id shown in the 2D plan (1F = 1 — view_get_state / draw_list_stories list them); renderMode = solid-edge | solid | wireframe | xray | realistic (3D). story alone switches to the 2D plan, renderMode alone switches to 3D. focus = an object id (obstacle, hole, vent, fire, device) or focusXb = a box to centre the 2D / 3D camera on. hideObjects / showObjects = obstacle ids to hide or show again one by one (a wall group goes together). smokePreview = the 3D smoke preview (rough pre-run flow, not FDS results): {enabled, running, quality fast|normal|fine, speed 0 (max)|1|2|4, density 0.1–10, restart}. To show / hide layers use view_set_layers; for a screenshot use capture_view.

story.description: Story id shown in the 2D plan (1F = 1, not a 0-based index)

focus.description: Object id to centre the view on (obstacle, hole, vent, fire, device)

focusXb.description: Box [x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2] (m) to centre the view on

showObjects.description: Hidden obstacle ids to show again

smokePreview.description: 3D smoke preview settings (only the given keys change)

restart.description: true = restart the preview from t = 0

tools.name: view_count_elements
tools.description: Count model elements whether shown or hidden — answers "how many sprinkler heads / air terminals / ducts / doors?". Sprinklers are reported by source: IFC geometry heads (imported model, geometry only — not hydraulic SPR heads), SPR pipe-network heads (hydraulic calculation) and FDS deck sprinklers / detectors; HVAC likewise: IFC air terminals, ducts, dampers, fans vs HVAC-module diffusers, grilles, air handlers, ducts vs FDS HVAC terminals. Also piping, electrical, equipment and per-layer counts (walls, doors, windows, slabs …). topic = a layer or group name (sprinkler, hvac, pipe, electrical, equipment, mep, architecture; Korean names too) to report only that part; default all. Read-only.

topic.description: Layer or group to count (default: all)

tools.name: results_open
tools.description: Load the results of a deck into the app's result viewer and open it — the same as the viewer's Load SMV: reads the .smv next to the deck (named by its &HEAD CHID), its &GEOM geometry, grid and the HRR curve, replacing the results shown now. Then list the datasets with result_get_state, load one with result_set_active_dataset and look with capture_view {view:"result"}. fdsPath defaults to the project deck / last run. Display only (no files are written). Live app only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: onto_search
tools.description: Find ontology ids by keyword in Korean or English — call {"query":"open boundary"}. Use it only when you don't know the type id, tool name or rule id (the L0 map lists every type). Each hit shows the id for onto_describe {"id":"<id>"}; weak hits are marked.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "방화문", "sprinkler activation", "open boundary"

tools.name: onto_describe
tools.description: Explain one ontology concept — call {"id":"Door"} ("detail":"full" for every section): a type, property ('Door.width'), tool ('add_door'), rule ('SPR-012'), term or playbook. Gives units/defaults/FDS keys, links, tools, rules with their instruction and common mistakes. Describe a type when the user did not give its values; describe a rule only when a violation cites it.

tools.name: onto_neighbors
tools.description: Follow ontology links up to depth 2 — call {"id":"SprinklerDevice"} for a type or {"id":"Door/Door_D1"} for a project object. Use it to see what something depends on or affects across modules (sprinkler → device → PROP → RAMP). Filter with rels (link ids, or fk|function|containment).

id.description: Type or interface id ('SprinklerHead'), or a project object 'Type/id'

rels.description: Only these link ids (inverse ids count), or fk / function / containment

tools.name: query_objects
tools.description: List project objects of one ontology type or interface with their real ids — call {"type":"Door","select":["*"]} when a tool needs an id no list tool shows. where: {field: value} or {field: {op: value}} (eq|ne|lt|lte|gt|gte|in|contains|exists); select: fields; aggregate: {count:true} or {groupBy:"field"}.

type.description: Ontology type or interface id (a label like '방화문' also works)

select.description: Fields to return (dot paths, '$title'); ['*'] = whole record. Default: type, id, title

aggregate.description: Return only a count, or counts grouped by a field

tools.name: onto_validate
tools.description: Rule check of the whole project — call {"scope":"project"} (or {}) once after your changes; it includes every validate_project check, so do not call both. {"scope":"object","target":{"type":"Door","id":"Door_D1"}} checks one object; {"scope":"proposed_change","change":{"tool":"add_door","args":{…}}} dry-runs a tool and reports only NEW violations (nothing applied).

scope.description: What to check (default: proposed_change when change is given, object when target is given, otherwise project)

change.description: scope proposed_change: the tool call to try
